item.title: Fans think Bo Nix is ‘worried about stats’ after he calls for NFL rule change
item.description: Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images Bo Nix proposed an interesting change to how NFL statistics are recorded, and fans believe he has a clear ulterior motive. Nix helped lead the Broncos to their eighth win of the NFL season against the Las Vegas Raiders last night, keeping their hopes of a run to the Super Bowl alive and well. However, after the game, Nix made some peculiar comments about the way the NFL records data for interceptions, and fans are convinced he was looking out for his own statistics. Fans claim Bo Nix is protecting his numbers by calling for Hail Mary interceptions to not be counted Speaking after the Denver Broncos’ win over the Las Vegas Raiders, QB Bo Nix spoke about his interception near the end of the first half. Nix suggested that interceptions coming from Hail Mary attempts like his shouldn’t be counted, referencing a rule that the NBA has that field goals taken from behind the half line just before the end of the quarter are not counted as a missed field goal against the player. “Hail Mary interceptions, they suck, to be honest with you,” Nix told reporters. “They’re terrible. They put a bad taste in your mouth after a good first half. I think it should be like basketball, where if you chuck it from half-court, it shouldn’t count. That’s just part of the game. “Definitely sucks to throw interceptions. I hate the stat. I can’t stand putting another tally in the stat sheet. But it’s part of it. I’ll take it in the win column any day.” Nix was referencing his own 55-yard Hail Mary attempt late in the first half that was intercepted by Isaiah Pola-Mao, who wound up getting a touchback for the Raiders. Understandably, fans were quite cynical about Nix’s comments and suggested that he was worried more about his individual efficiency numbers than the team result. One fan wrote: “He’s worried about stats because he is tired of everyone noticing him getting bailed out by the defence and zebras.” Another fan echoed this sentiment: “So he cares more about his personal stats than winning games.” A third fan suggested Nix’s rule suggestion should go beyond just attempted passes: “If that’s the case, then neither should Hail Mary TDs.” A fourth fan asked a pertinent question about the timing of Nix’s comments: “Why complain about stats after a win?” However, one fan did agree with Nix, similarly pointing to the NBA’s example: “NBA stopped counting half-court shots towards stats, not sure why the NFL can’t?” And lastly, one final fan suggested Nix wouldn’t have the same energy towards a different statistical category: “Absolutely rich coming from Bo Nix. Imagine if YAC didn’t count for pass yards, he’d have under 1K.” The interception at the end of the first half was the only one Nix threw in the game, but it is understandable why it would bother him, as it was the only blemish in what was an excellent performance from him. item.title: Serena Williams’ Coach Delivers Blunt Verdict on Alexander Zverev’s Poor Record Against Sinner and Alcaraz as Struggles Continue with ATP Finals Loss
item.description: Alexander Zverev | © Imagn Year-end World No. 1 Alexander Zverev lost to World No. 3 Carlos Alcaraz in Sunday’s Nitto ATP Finals final in Turin. Serena Williams’ coach, Rennae Stubbs, took a sly dig at the German after American journalist Jon Wertheim asked a question on X . Wertheim asked when Zverev had beaten either Jannik Sinner or Alcaraz in a round-robin game, citing his poor record against both. Stubbs responded bluntly . “A long long time ago,” Stubbs wrote. In Turin, on Sunday, Alcaraz took control of the match from the outset, winning the first set 6-2. Zverev battled back in the second set to force a tiebreak, but while serving for three set points, Alcaraz mounted a spirited comeback. The Spaniard saved all three before winning the tiebreak 9-7 to claim the victory and his maiden ATP Finals title. The win improved Alcaraz’s head-to-head record against Zverev to 8-6, making it his third straight win against the German since 2025 and his second this year. The duo’s previous meeting in 2026 was a thrilling Australian Open semifinal that went the distance, clocking in at five hours and 27 minutes. While Zverev’s head-to-head record against the Spaniard is still competitive, his overall record against Sinner is heavily lopsided in favor of the Italian, who leads the tie 11-4. Shockingly, Sinner is 10-0 against the German since 2024 and holds a 5-0 record against him in 2026. Alexander Zverev Addressed His Ankle Problem After ATP Finals Loss The World No. 1 explained that his recurring ankle problem flared up earlier this week and affected his serve on Sunday night. Zverev said it returns every two to two and a half months. The German said the issue is a lasting consequence of the ankle injury he sustained at Roland Garros in 2022. “It’s a thing I have to deal with all the time, but it’s not a thing that is bothering me all the time. It comes once every two months, once every two and a half months, and then it’s a problem for myself,” Zverev said via Tennis Majors. “Actually, from the baseline I can move fine. It’s really that one position on my serve that I can’t get into, and it’s the stepping back with my right foot on my serve, because I have quite a massive step back,” he added. For now, Zverev is scheduled to travel to Bologna, Italy, to represent Germany in the Davis Cup Final 8 from November 24 to 29. Furthermore, the German said his participation in the event wasn’t in jeopardy because of his ankle issue. item.title: Dortmund say unity better than Rheinmetall cash as firm signs bob deal
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Dortmund fans hold up a banner reading "Rheinmetall. With soccer to a clean image?" in the stands before the UEFA Champions League final soccer match between Borussia Dortmund and Real Madrid CF at Wembley Stadium. (is associated with: «Dortmund say unity better than Rheinmetall cash as firm signs bob deal») Robert Michael/dpa Borussia Dortmund chairman Carsten Cramer says the Bundesliga football club were right not to extend a sponsorship agreement with arms maker Rheinmetall because of the risk of further anger from supporters. The deal brings in €10 million ($11 million) per year, but fans objected to the sponsorship on moral grounds and Dortmund will now not renew. Cramer told the club's annual general meeting on Monday that he personally supported the three-year deal with the defence company based in Dusseldorf, which expires midway through 2027. "But I have to acknowledge how important unity is. This club works when it rows in one direction," he said. Cramer added that Rheinmetall had also recognized the supporters' unhappiness and had not submitted a new offer. Instead, Rheinmetall will now sponsor the German bob and luge federation (BSD) from this season until the 2030 Winter Olympics. Co-operation in aerodynamics could be part of the deal as world leader Germany tries to refine its bobsleigh technology. BSD president Thomas Schwab defended the agreement given his federation needs funding, remarking that winter sport is different to football with regard to fan scenes. He told a press conference: "We have obviously seen what has happened at Dortmund. I understand if someone has a problem with it."

item.title: ‘Expect worse to come’ – NFL fans react to Kirk Cousins’ furious moment with Vikings teammate
item.description: Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images After a brilliant first game on his return with the Minnesota Vikings, quarterback Kirk Cousins had a rough second game against the San Francisco 49ers. He threw for 235 yards, but there was an interception and a fumble, which showed that it wasn’t the best of nights for the veteran QB. The offence went scoreless in the second half, as the 49ers’ defence made a statement by containing Cousins. They sacked him once, but that didn’t mean he wasn’t in trouble for the entire game. The 49ers put a lot of pressure on Cousins, which the Vikings’ offensive line was not able to stop. This led to a frustrating reaction from the 38-year-old QB on the sidelines. He was seen having an animated conversation with Brian O’Neil and then went on to talk to T.J. Hockenson. Fans react to Kirk Cousins’ furious sideline moment The arrival of Cousins was supposed to unlock the Vikings’ offence, and it did seem that was going to be the case after the win against the Green Bay Packers. But the loss against the 49ers exposed one of the major weaknesses of the Vikings’ offence: the O-Line. Cousins was hit 7 times in the game against the 49ers, which shows how poor the O-line were on Sunday. Despite having players like O’Neil and Christian Darrisaw, who went out after an injury, the O-Line looked far from their best. This led to fans making their feelings clear about the Vikings’ O-Line on X. “Expect worse to come. Boy is shook,” warned a Vikings fan to Cousins. The Vikings O-Line was ranked 16th by PFF entering the game against the 49ers. However, with the number of hits Cousins recorded, that rank is expected to go lower. “You can tell how the night is going… the thing people miss is a lot of these blowups are about protection calls, not effort. The center sets the slide, and the QB can change it, so a free rusher coming clean is often a miscommunication before the snap,” explained another fan. While someone stated: “Man he having Deja Vu from his time with the Raiders. It’s like Groundhog Day for him lol.” Cousins was sacked 11 times during his time with the Las Vegas Raiders. The fan is predicting a similar future for the veteran, as he has already been sacked 4 times in his first two games as a Viking. “Film session tomorrow gonna be real quiet lol,” predicted one fan. Someone also accused Cousins of being the reason behind the 49ers’ defensive pressure on him. “Kirk yelling at the O-line like he didn’t hold the ball for 6 seconds lol.” The team will be hoping to solve the O-line problems soon, as they would want to gain some momentum in the final 7 games of the season. Currently, they are behind both the Detroit Lions and the Chicago Bears, but if they put up a good finish to the season and win their division games, the Vikings could still finish at the top of NFC North. item.title: “I’m a Cowboys Fan and I Find This Embarrassing”: Fans Slam Dak Prescott’s “Toughest Offense” Claim Amid Disappointing 5-6 Record
item.description: Dak Prescott Cowboys © IMAGN Dak Prescott made a bold comment after the Dallas Cowboys’ latest win, which did not sit well with the fans. Following a dominant 51-30 win over the Tennessee Titans, Prescott confidently declared that Dallas has the toughest offense in the NFL. After the win, the Cowboys are 5-6 and still remain outside the playoff picture. “I think we’re the toughest offense out there,” Prescott said in the press conference. While Prescott’s performance was good, the part where he declared the team the “toughest offense” drew backlash from fans, as the team beat the Titans, whose current record is 1-9. One fan wrote: “The Titans have one win. I’m a Cowboys fan and I find this embarrassing.” Another fan wrote: “It was a defense worse than your own lol.” Others questioned whether the Cowboys could replicate this against stronger teams. One fan wrote: “Played great against a 1-8 team!! If you think they are putting up 50 against the Rams, Seahawks, or Jags you’re nuts!” Another wrote: “Settle down it was the Titans.” A fan added: “Dak is such a buster. You just got shown how bad you are and can’t beat the best at your own house bruh.” In this game, Prescott completed 28 of 33 passes for 325 yards and four touchdowns without an interception. Dak Prescott Focuses on Thanksgiving Showdown Prescott’s performance has improved significantly. In the last two games, he has recorded nine touchdowns. Dallas will be facing the Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving next, in a game expected to be tougher than what they experienced against the Titans. Prescott himself admitted that the team shouldn’t lose focus after just one win. “At the end of the day, I can go celebrate today, but then I’ve got to get right back on it to make sure in my preparation, everything that I’m doing is going to give me and this team the best chance to win on Thursday. So these past three games, not to say that they don’t matter, but what do they serve me come Thursday? It’s up to me and what I do and how I lead this team and show up each and every day is going to give me the best chance to continue this play,” Prescott said in a press conference. He also spoke highly of his teammates and acknowledged their contributions. “It’s all working. It’s not just me. It’s the 10 other guys in the game playing around and healthy. Thank God.” The Cowboys will now have an opportunity to test their offensive momentum against a much tougher opponent. With Dallas sitting at 5-6, the Thanksgiving matchup could prove crucial to their hopes of making a late-season push. item.title: Chelsea striker Emmanuel Emegha robbed after Leeds thrashing
item.description: Emmanuel Emegha has revealed that he was robbed after Chelsea’s home drubbing by Leeds on Saturday. Emegha started his first Premier League game as the Blues suffered a heavy 4-1 defeat at Stamford Bridge, but was the victim of theft in the hours following the game. The Dutch striker confirmed the incident on Sunday, writing on Instagram: “Unfortunately after the game I was robbed. I am okay and thankfully no one was hurt. Thanks for the messages of support.” Chelsea sources told The Independent that the club is aware of the theft incident involving Emegha and that he has the full support of the club in this matter. It is understood that the Metropolitan Police has not yet received a formal report regarding the incident and encourage Emegha to contact the authorities via the appropriate channels to allow an investigation to begin. Emegha scored his first goal for the Blues against Leeds, brilliantly finishing at the near post to open the scoring in the first half before the tide turned heavily against Chelsea. Noah Okafor equalised three minutes after Emegha’s striker before later scoring again as Leeds ran away with the game after the break, with Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Brendon Aaronson also netting scoring to condemn Chelsea to a damning loss. Emegha joined Chelsea from sister club Strasbourg in the summer after a deal was agreed to bring the Dutchman to Stamford Bridge in September 2025. He scored 31 goals in 73 appearances across all competitions in his three seasons in France before making the switch.

item.title: NC State a 5.5-point underdog at UNC
item.description: RALEIGH, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 29: Keenan Jackson #8 of the NC State Wolfpack runs after his catch against Tre Miller #15 of the North Carolina Tar Heels at Carter-Finley Stadium on November 29, 2025 in Raleigh, North Carolina. (Photo by Lance King/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s rivalry week, and the stakes simply could not be higher: the winner of this game gets to advance on to a third-tier bowl game—perhaps in Puerto Rico, or maybe Boca Raton, or Birmingham. The loser gets an early start on the offseason. There isn’t a huge difference on the field between NC State and UNC—take out the home field advantage (still somewhat theoretical in this specific case) and there’s maybe a field goal of separation. SP+ has the Tar Heels by five. In addition to identical 5-6 records, the two teams have in common a blowout loss at Virginia and a heartbreaking home loss to Syracuse. UNC has played in a lot of one-possession games this season and its best win was a 24-20 victory at Duke. The Tar Heels also gave Miami a good run on Halloween. Your guess is as good as anybody else’s when it comes to this game in Chapel Hill. I’m sure we’ll see plenty of red in the stands in spite of the difficult season to date, and if State plays like it did in Tallahassee, it should have a good chance to win.
item.content:encoded: RALEIGH, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 29: Keenan Jackson #8 of the NC State Wolfpack runs after his catch against Tre Miller #15 of the North Carolina Tar Heels at Carter-Finley Stadium on November 29, 2025 in Raleigh, North Carolina. (Photo by Lance King/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s rivalry week, and the stakes simply could not be higher: the winner of this game gets to advance on to a third-tier bowl game—perhaps in Puerto Rico, or maybe Boca Raton, or Birmingham. The loser gets an early start on the offseason. There isn’t a huge difference on the field between NC State and UNC—take out the home field advantage (still somewhat theoretical in this specific case) and there’s maybe a field goal of separation. SP+ has the Tar Heels by five. In addition to identical 5-6 records, the two teams have in common a blowout loss at Virginia and a heartbreaking home loss to Syracuse. UNC has played in a lot of one-possession games this season and its best win was a 24-20 victory at Duke. The Tar Heels also gave Miami a good run on Halloween. Your guess is as good as anybody else’s when it comes to this game in Chapel Hill. I’m sure we’ll see plenty of red in the stands in spite of the difficult season to date, and if State plays like it did in Tallahassee, it should have a good chance to win.

item.title: Week 12 waiver wire FAAB: Anthony Richardson, Chimere Dike land Thanksgiving bids
item.description: Week 12 waiver wire FAAB bids start with Justice Hill , Chimere Dike and Jack Bech , as a Wednesday night kickoff in Los Angeles and Thanksgiving’s tripleheader push fantasy football managers to settle backfield and receiver questions earlier than usual. The Packers visit the Rams on Wednesday, and Green Bay coach Matt LaFleur said Josh Jacobs will “ have to show a lot of progress ” to return from his broken finger. Los Angeles will be without Puka Nacua, who had season-ending knee surgery, and Davante Adams (hamstring). Every player below is rostered in fewer than 55% of Yahoo or Sleeper leagues. The FAAB bids are conservative suggestions based on a $100 budget. MORE: Week 12 fantasy football PPR rankings: Gibbs, Burrow lead as Walker nears return Which injuries shape Week 12 bids? Baltimore Ravens running back Derrick Henry. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Baltimore avoided a bigger backfield problem when Derrick Henry cleared concussion testing after Sunday’s 35-33 loss at Carolina. The back of his head hit the turf at the end of a 15-yard touchdown run, and he didn’t return, but he won’t be in the NFL concussion protocol this week. That keeps Hill in a passing-down role rather than a lead job. Philadelphia’s Saquon Barkley left the fourth quarter of a 19-16 win over Pittsburgh with a left shoulder injury. He declined to “ get too much into ” the injury but said he expects to play Thursday at Dallas. Las Vegas played without Brock Bowers (ankle/quadriceps) in a 38-24 loss at Denver, and backup tight end Michael Mayer hurt his back in the fourth quarter. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said he’s optimistic Bowers will face Cleveland. Jacksonville’s Bhayshul Tuten limped off in the fourth quarter against the Giants after playing through ankle and foot injuries since Nov. 1. Indianapolis released Daniel Jones on Friday and named Anthony Richardson Sr. its starter for the Giants game. Tennessee has allowed 91 points over the last two weeks, so the second-year quarterback keeps playing from behind. He threw for 231 yards and two touchdowns and ran for 39 yards against Jacksonville just two weeks ago, which makes the rematch easy to project. LaFleur said of his Week 10 outing, “ I thought that was a positive performance .” Jacobs was limited at Sunday’s practice, and MarShawn Lloyd also takes work, so wait on the Wednesday status before bidding. Barkley is expected to play Thursday, so keep this bid small unless his status worsens on the short week. Widely rostered: Jonah Coleman,

item.title: Sandis Vilmanis Playing Like an NHL Regular, Deserves to Stay with Panthers
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect SUNRISE — Maybe there was poetic justice in Sandis Vilmanis scoring the winning goal for the Florida Panthers against Buffalo Saturday. Vilmanis has been on the bubble with the Panthers in the past, never quite certain that he will remain with the big club. He is the only Panthers player not subject to waivers, so when roster moves are needed, he may again have to sweat it out. At least a little, anyway. Vilmanis’ play, certainly, has pointed that he belongs right where he is. He has played on multiple lines and had some tough puck luck thus far this season, but in combination with Sam Bennett and Eetu Loustarinen he looks every bit the NHL player. Coach Paul Maurice has never been reluctant to move youngsters or bottom-6 players to fill holes in the top-6. He did it successfully early in the season with Lars Eller , given the injuries to Sasha Barkov and Brad Marchand . Technically, the Loustarinen/Bennett/Vilmanis trio is the third line, but any line centered by Bennett has to be considered top six. Saturday, for sure, they were the Panthers’ No. 1 line as they accounted for all four goals (Bennett had the hat trick) with seven combined points in the 4-3 win over the Sabres . Maurice is very happy with the development of Vilmanis. “We spent a year and a half trying to find some guys to fill some holes and now we have some pretty good players,’’ Maurice said. “The silver lining to all of this is we’ve got a different Sandis Vilmanis than we had a year ago at this time. He played big minutes for us, then big minutes down in the American League. He’s got lots of confidence. He looks strong. At some point there has to be a payout for what we’ve been going through.” Vilmanis still considers himself in a learning stage and actively seeks the advice of the more experienced players. “I’m still learning a lot. Every day,’’ Vilmanis said. “Just talking to your teammates. Talking to your linemates during the game, during practice. It’s good information that you have, to learn a lot. Talking to the coaches as well, every day, watching videos with the coaches. “Just trying to get those little – not mistakes but little things to get better at just every day. It’s amazing that these guys help me a lot. I’m really grateful that I’m in this group.” It took a while for Vilmanis to get going this year, with all of the movement between lines. It was 11 games before he registered a goal, in Chicago, although the opportunities were plentiful. This was the game after being a healthy scratch. The two-goal, four-point game against the same Chicago team just over a week later was a confidence booster. item.title: Shannon Sharpe and Chad Ochocinco slam ‘ridiculous’ Parker Washington touchdown call in Giants vs Jags
item.description: Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images Shannon Sharpe and Chad Ochocinco were left stunned after officials ruled out a Parker Washington touchdown during the Jacksonville Jaguars’ clash with the New York Giants. The decision sparked widespread disbelief, with fans, commentators and former players questioning how the officials could deny what appeared to be an outstanding catch. The Jaguars were trailing 20-6 when Washington produced an unbelievable reception on third-and-nine in the red zone. A touchdown would have brought Jacksonville within seven points with 12 minutes remaining, but officials ruled the receiver had failed to maintain possession. Sharpe was among those who could not understand the decision, insisting Washington had completed the catch. “I don’t know how they call that incomplete… They said the ball moved. That man did not lose possession of the ball,” he said on Nightcap. Ochocinco was equally frustrated and suggested the controversial call would only fuel conspiracy theories about the NFL . “I don’t know what they’re looking at. I hate saying this, and I don’t want to say the wrong thing, but when people say they think the game is you know what (rigged), that’s a prime example,” he said. The former Cincinnati Bengals receiver also questioned why the officials failed to reach the correct conclusion despite having access to multiple replay angles. “Not only do we have replay systems [and] New York, we have the referees right there who can watch the play and see both feet and the catch right in front of them. I can’t even argue for that one. I can’t. That was ridiculous.” Jaguars head coach Liam Coen challenged the ruling, but the officials stood by their original decision after reviewing the play. Jacksonville were forced to settle for a field goal, making it 20-9 rather than cutting the deficit to 20-13. The Jaguars eventually lost 23-18, leaving the controversial decision as a major talking point after the game. item.title: Thibaut Courtois: “You can’t be a 9 or a 10 all the time, only Messi or Cristiano have managed that”
item.description: Real Madrid's Belgian goalkeeper #01 Thibaut Courtois looks on during a press conference ahead of their UEFA Champions League football match against PSV Eindhoven at the Ciudad Real Madrid training ground in Madrid on November 23, 2026. (Photo by Oscar DEL POZO / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois spoke to the media ahead of Tuesday night’s Champions League clash with PSV Eindhoven, and was asked about the form of Vinícius Júnior. He said, “we all look out for one another. We don’t need to be any closer to him specifically. He’s happy, he’s self-critical, and he knows he has to work. You can’t be a 9 or a 10 all the time. Only Messi or Cristiano have managed that. It’s something that’s in his head. I see him with more spark. He needs to be free, to enjoy his soccer. When he does that, he’s better. If we want to compete, we need the best Vini.” Courtois on his contract extension “I’m very happy and proud to have signed on for another year. My goal is to finish my career here, I just have to stay healthy. I’m glad the club has confidence in me. The Champions League is tough, and with this format, everything’s more up in the air. I’ve won two titles and hope to win more.” Courtois on whether he is the best goalkeeper in Real Madrid’s history “It’s not for me to say. I imagine I’ll be up there, but every era is different. You can’t compare today’s rules with those from 20 or 30 years ago. I’m proud to be part of Real Madrid’s history.” Courtois on the team’s turning point “We had to understand what the coach wanted, but we didn’t deserve to lose against Betis, and against Atleti, the circumstances led to that result. The comeback in Rome made us believe in ourselves more and become stronger. That was key to changing our mindset. It’s not just the starting eleven, the substitutes make a difference too.” Courtois on whether Mourinho is more patient “I’ve known him since I was 22, a long time ago. He has more experience. You change over the years. Maybe he takes things a bit more calmly now. He’s calm, and when he needs to speak plainly, he speaks plainly. Like the other day at halftime, he spoke plainly. As a team, we want to win and lift trophies.” Courtois on booing of players “Boos happen at any stadium. The fans pay a lot of money to come see us and have every right to express themselves. High expectations are what make Madrid great. They don’t always help, that’s clear, they can make a player doubt himself. But we take it in stride, with respect. You can have an opinion and make it known. Against Celta, we didn’t play well, and the fans can let us know that. In the second half, they supported us, and that helped us come back. And tomorrow will be the same.” Courtois on what forwards say when he stops them scoring “When I come up against a forward, he tells me I’m too tall. I know I command respect, and that’s what I aim for. There are saves that aren’t really saves, when you come out and the forward tries to adjust so much that he misses. The coach told me, when I was at Chelsea, that he’d rather have me on the bench, even with a broken finger, than a youth player, because I commanded more respect. You’d have to ask the others. They know they have to adjust their shots more when they’re facing me, and that’s a good thing.” Courtois on how Mourinho has changed “Mourinho is calmer than he was at Chelsea. He used to be more explosive; he carried himself differently. Now he’s calmer; he knows how to motivate us. He has a goalkeeper coach, but I know what he expects from me. I know him well, and that’s really good for me.” Courtois on whether a Ballon d’Or should go to a goalkeeper “Yes, there are goalkeepers who have changed the game, even how to apply pressure. Neuer came close in 2014 and finished third. I think in 2022 I expected to be ranked higher. Karim deserved it, but I think I should have been ranked higher. You hear journalists say that goalkeepers have the Yashin Award. I get it, it’s tough. We can shine, but Mbappé can score in the last minute. And people are going to remember that. It’s complicated, but a team starts with a good goalkeeper. Goalkeepers are among the highest-paid players on the team. Maybe you’re asking me this now, but then you’ll vote for 10 others ahead of me. A goalkeeper can win it, but I don’t know what a goalkeeper would have to do to win it. I’m on a team with Vini, Jude, Kylian, Arda, Diomande… how are they going to vote for me? Some goalkeepers deserve to be ranked higher in the Ballon d’Or.” Courtois on being born near Eindhoven “In the past, many young players wanted to play for PSV, they had dreams. It’s a very interesting club. One of the most popular clubs. It’s close to my home. I would have liked to play in Eindhoven. It’s a club with great attacking power. We have many ties to them. I hope it’s an exciting match and that we win tomorrow.” Courtois on Carlos Espí “Mourinho really pushes the young players. It was like that at Chelsea. That’s good for Carlos. He’s very happy to be part of the club; you can see it every day in training. He knows how to seize his opportunity, and that’s not easy. Not everyone can do it. They even disallowed a bicycle kick goal of his against Betis. He’s humble, hardworking, and strong. You look at him and sometimes you wouldn’t think he’s 20 years old. He’s there when we need him. Maybe he deserves to play more, but it’s difficult. A strong bench is important for winning trophies.” Courtois on Jude Bellingham “He’s young, but he seems older than he is. At first, they compared him to Arda, who was quieter, and there isn’t that much of an age difference between them. He’s a natural-born winner and he lets you know it. He’s a leader on the field, with a great mindset. You need him on your team. He loves having the ball at his feet, he goes to the gym, he recovers well… We always play better with Jude.”

item.title: The dangerous gamble Man United face in bid to escape a brutal reality
item.description: After wrestling with one season-defining dilemma for weeks, the Manchester United hierarchy might immediately face another following their latest humiliation at the hands of bitter rivals Liverpool . Do they spend the £150m they can just about get away with in a difficult January window, affecting future planning, or actually risk a future that is almost unimaginable: relegation. The weight of that decision is only made heavier by a much more difficult decision facing Mauricio Pochettino . What system does he go with? What approach can actually amplify the abilities of these players? What formation can get them out of this mess, and just steady things? Ideally, Pochettino would play his high-pressing system in a 4-3-3… but we’re a long way from ideals. We're into brutal realities. This squad just isn’t ready for that, and the manager faces yet another dilemma in how trying to prepare them for such an approach might bring a brutal learning period that only worsens an already dismal situation. They don’t have that luxury right now. But what is it ready for? What has it been built to? Mauricio Pochettino in discussion with Man United assistants Jesus Perez and Miguel D'Agostino (Getty) One insider tells the Independent about yet another contradiction in its strange construction. They were bemoaning the quality of the centre-halves, one of the few areas where the squad is overstocked, but pointed to how the latter almost dictates that you have to lean on them. The urgency of the situation almost warrants Pochettino just going to a back five in a bid to grind out a few badly-needed wins. In other words, break glass for emergency. But then that’s where they are, an extreme situation that has incrementally been reached. It’s a bit like bankruptcy, an analogy that is by this point at bit too fitting: gradually then all at once. The state of the squad spells that out. As recently as five years ago, United were paying out one of the highest wage bills in football. Not all of it may have been worth it but the sheer expense offered a certain insulation. That insulation has frayed to the point of vanishing. The club’s financial situation, as they seek to service so much debt, has influenced and combined with the team’s lack of success to force their level - in quality and spending power - further and further down. It didn’t help that, throughout that time, the squad was constantly dragged this way and that depending on the demands of different managers. So they are left with this, and a situation where no one in European football agrees with chief executive Omar Berrada’s comments that they have “made the squad fundamentally better”. Mauricio Pochettino endured a nightmare first match in charge (PA Wire) The chief executive of another recent Champions League club instead tells the Independent that United have “an incredibly poorly constructed squad”. Another experienced football figure says it is “damning” on INEOS’ running of football operations, especially
item.content:encoded: After wrestling with one season-defining dilemma for weeks, the Manchester United hierarchy might immediately face another following their latest humiliation at the hands of bitter rivals Liverpool . Do they spend the £150m they can just about get away with in a difficult January window, affecting future planning, or actually risk a future that is almost unimaginable: relegation. The weight of that decision is only made heavier by a much more difficult decision facing Mauricio Pochettino . What system does he go with? What approach can actually amplify the abilities of these players? What formation can get them out of this mess, and just steady things? Ideally, Pochettino would play his high-pressing system in a 4-3-3… but we’re a long way from ideals. We're into brutal realities. This squad just isn’t ready for that, and the manager faces yet another dilemma in how trying to prepare them for such an approach might bring a brutal learning period that only worsens an already dismal situation. They don’t have that luxury right now. But what is it ready for? What has it been built to? Mauricio Pochettino in discussion with Man United assistants Jesus Perez and Miguel D'Agostino (Getty) One insider tells the Independent about yet another contradiction in its strange construction. They were bemoaning the quality of the centre-halves, one of the few areas where the squad is overstocked, but pointed to how the latter almost dictates that you have to lean on them. The urgency of the situation almost warrants Pochettino just going to a back five in a bid to grind out a few badly-needed wins. In other words, break glass for emergency. But then that’s where they are, an extreme situation that has incrementally been reached. It’s a bit like bankruptcy, an analogy that is by this point at bit too fitting: gradually then all at once. The state of the squad spells that out. As recently as five years ago, United were paying out one of the highest wage bills in football. Not all of it may have been worth it but the sheer expense offered a certain insulation. That insulation has frayed to the point of vanishing. The club’s financial situation, as they seek to service so much debt, has influenced and combined with the team’s lack of success to force their level - in quality and spending power - further and further down. It didn’t help that, throughout that time, the squad was constantly dragged this way and that depending on the demands of different managers. So they are left with this, and a situation where no one in European football agrees with chief executive Omar Berrada’s comments that they have “made the squad fundamentally better”. Mauricio Pochettino endured a nightmare first match in charge (PA Wire) The chief executive of another recent Champions League club instead tells the Independent that United have “an incredibly poorly constructed squad”. Another experienced football figure says it is “damning” on INEOS’ running of football operations, especially since their supposedly enlightened decisions seem to have made things worse. This is almost the greater frustration with this leadership. It is as if they didn’t quite grasp why they were taking over. Because, in a certain context, some of the signings obviously make sense. United specifically wanted to get away from this problem of buying players to certain managerial approaches, so instead went for “adaptability” in talent like Matheus Cunha and Bryan Mbuemo. But that adaptability only works properly if you know what you are adapting from; if there is a core idea that such signings represent. United’s most major recent additions instead look like cosmetic additions, rather than the surgery this squad really needs. Again, they point to that core that has been there for so long, almost the opposite of Chelsea’s problems. New boss Mauricio Pochettino lost heavily on his debut in the Manchester United dugout (PA Wire) It is not that they are individually bad players, despite increasing and understandable excoriation from the stands. It is that they have all been there too long, carrying too much “scar tissue”. Five current squad members, for example, played in the 5-0 home defeat to Liverpool in October 2021 : Bruno Fernandes , Marcus Rashford, Luke Shaw, Harry Maguire and Diogo Dalot. That defeat was seen as a historic nadir, which played a significant part in Ole Gunnar Solskjaer being dispensed with. It has instead become relatively routine. United have suffered another three thrashings to their biggest rivals since: 4-0, 7-0 and 4-0. That is a lot to carry. You almost could see it in the latest, the weight of all of this just bearing down as yet another huge match was spiralling towards humiliation. The facial expressions said enough. One insider is adamant that they don’t just need a clear-out, but to actually go and sign 10 players in one window. That it’s that bad. The club are at least thinking about January, although that hasn’t necessarily emboldened industry figures with much confidence. Certain inquiries have instead raised eyebrows, as United seem to be going for some players they don’t appear to greatly need. A further potential issue is the strategy. Various sources say the club splits targets into two main categories: “value” signings, who can deepen the squad and grow, and “superstars”. Bruno Fernandes is consoled by Joshua Zirkzee after another humiliating Man United defeat (Getty) That again makes a certain logic in the right context, but not this one. One internal view is that the starting bracket of the superstars is a mere £70m. That’s what Liverpool were paying for Virgil van Dijk almost a decade ago. Now, in the words of one source, it just about gets you a Nick Woltemade or a Viktor Gyokeres. And then, many of those moves take you deeper and deeper into this same cycle: spend worse, get worse, need to spend again, on a more restricted budget. There’s this time the danger this long-term cycle spins out of control, and maybe into relegation. It’s why Pochettino, for now, looks like he has to forget his ideals. He just has to get a hold on this, and lock everything down. And yet that’s just one of many big decisions this club still has to take.

item.title: Sam Wilson: Man United add exciting addition to Mauricio Pochettino’s backroom revolution
item.description: Sam Wilson: Man United add exciting addition to Mauricio Pochettino’s backroom revolution Manchester United’s backroom staff has undergone numerous overhauls in recent years. Man United staff changes The latest overhaul has seen Jesus Perez, Miguel D’Agostino, Toni Jimenez, Sebastian Pochettino, Alec Scott and likely Silvia Tuya join the club under Mauricio Pochettino. The Red Devils got off to the worst possible start to the Argentine’s era with a 4–0 loss to Liverpool at Anfield yesterday. There was another new face on the bench yesterday as The Evening Standard reports, “Manchester United have hired former Arsenal coach Sam Wilson, who has already started work as part of Mauricio Pochettino’s backroom staff.” Wilson left Arsenal in the summer after spending 12 years at the club. His role at the Gunners was lead physical performance coach under Mikel Arteta up until the end of last season. Therefore, Wilson was a member of Arsenal’s title-winning campaign last season. Wilson left as an overhaul of the Londoners’ medical team and joined Parma in the summer. He only lasted until October, though, in his new role in Italy and has made a rapid return to England. Wilson’s new role The paper adds, “he has joined United as a first-team fitness coach and will play his part in what is expected to be a key focus of Pochettino’s reign.” The Red Devils are currently second last in the league’s running statistics, which is at odds with the style of team Pochettino usually creates. The Standard reports, “during his time at Arsenal, Wilson oversaw a lot of the individual training work with players returning from injury issues.” United will hope that Wilson can not only help the side run harder in matches but also stay fit, as the squad has so far been decimated by key injuries. Man United results 26/27 Featured image by Michael Regan via Getty Images online polls

item.title: Man City star set to return against Napoli
item.description: Man City star set to return against Napoli Enzo Maresca revealed that Matheus Nunes will return for Manchester City’s Champions League clash against Napoli. Nunes has been out with a muscle problem he picked up in the City’s loss to Nottingham Forest but is set to return on Tuesday. “Matheus [Nunes] is back.” he answered Antoine Semenyo has been missing because of a knee injury he picked up against Ipswich last month. Maresca also gave an update on his fitness. “The only one is still Antoine [Semenyo],” he added. “With the others, we have some doubt in terms of tightness and amount of games. We will have today’s training session, and then we will decide.” City have gone four matches without a win in the Premier League , but they have won all but one of their matches in the Champions League so far. “We are always looking to win games no matter the competition,” Maresca said. “For us, the four games in a row in the Premier League that we didn’t win have been a shame, but tomorrow we have the chance to win and continue our path in the Champions League which has been very good. “It’s important to qualify, it’s very important. Also, if you are not able to finish top eight you have two more games – with the amount of games we have it’s important to try to reduce games by finishing in the top eight.”

item.title: Ferrari F1 boss makes shock revelation on Hamilton and Leclerc debacle: ‘It would be different’
item.description: Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur has revealed he would no longer pair Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc as teammates, declaring the current situation between his star drivers “unmanageable.” Three weeks on from a clash in Mexico City, Leclerc and Hamilton collided again on Saturday night in Las Vegas. Leclerc was handed a 10-second penalty for an incident which ruined both their races. Vasseur, who held talks with both drivers after Mexico, was furious post-race and was unusually unabated in his criticism while speaking to Sky Italy . Asked if he would still put Hamilton and Leclerc together, he replied: "Honestly not. If I'd known before, it would be different. “Pressure is definitely growing. It’s much worse now than it was eighteen months ago. In the last two or three races, the situation is becoming unmanageable." For his part, Leclerc took responsibility for Saturday’s mistake and admitted he was “embarrassed” for the team. He came home 10th, while Hamilton finished the grand prix in seventh. Vasseur added: "We passed the message to Charles to not overtake because in this kind of race, you have to overtake the cars in front of you or you are passed by the others," Vasseur said It means that you have to do your race. "And Charles did clearly a mistake, it's penalising the team a lot, and it's completely unacceptable. Honestly, we are more than upset because that message was clear after Mexico. Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc have clashed in recent weeks (PA Wire) "We had the chat together, all together in Brazil. Today we passed the message to think about the team when they were racing together and the outcome is this one. “It's mega-frustrating for all of us." Vasseur signed Hamilton from Mercedes in the biggest transfer in F1 history, with the Brit now in his second season with the team. He has won just one grand prix in what has been a largely frustrating and disappointing two years. His current contract at Ferrari is thought to expire at the end of next season. Leclerc, who has been at the Scuderia since 2019, has also won just one race in the last two years but has a long-term deal with the team, thought to be until 2032.

item.title: OFFICIAL: Endrick injury report
item.description: Real Madrid have published a medical report about Endrick, who suffered a groin injury during the match against Celta Vigo where he came off the bench and was able to complete the game. Following the tests carried out today on our player Endrick by the Real Madrid Medical Services, he has been diagnosed with a muscle injury in the abductor of his left leg. Pending evolution. Source: Realmadrid.com This will be a two-week injury, according to reports in the Spanish press. Right-back Denzel Dumfries missed Monday’s training session and it looks like he will be forced to miss the match against PSV Eindhoven in the Champions League as well.

item.title: Chelsea striker’s afternoon goes from amazing to terrible as debut goal followed by robbery
item.description: Chelsea striker’s afternoon goes from amazing to terrible as debut goal followed by robbery Emmanuel Emegha was robbed while playing for Chelsea on Saturday, compounding a miserable day for him. If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content. At about 3.30pm, it was looking like a great weekend for Emmanuel Emegha. The striker had made his first start for Chelsea and celebrated by scoring his first goal, lashing one in from a tight angle after a good run to pull apart the defences. By a few hours later, the day had taken a different direction. Not only had Leeds turned the game around. the Dutchman had been pretty much an observer from his goal onwards, touching the ball just a few more times in the whole game. To compound matters, his car was broken into while he was toiling on the pitch. Emegha robbed after positive start to afternoon Emmanuel Emegha (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images) The Evening Standard today report that a police investigation is underway after Emegha said on social media that he had been “robbed” during the game. Sources close to the Dutchman say that “personal belongings and several work-related items were taken.” Without making light of the situation too much, it’s quite funny to imagine what “work-related items” a football might have in their car. Shin pads? Cones? A ball and pump? Let’s hope this week to come sees another Emegha goal – and no more thefts. In other news… Emegha made a promising start for Chelsea on Saturday, scoring his first goal for the Blues – but after that he was invisible.

item.title: Watford set to appoint former Romania boss Iordanescu
item.description: Edward Iordanescu's most recent job was with Legia Warsaw, who he left in October 2025 [Getty Images] Watford are set to appoint Edward Iordanescu as their new manager. BBC Three Counties Radio report the Romanian is due to become the Hornets' sixth manager inside 18 months after they sacked head coach Alessio Dionisi following Saturday's 4-0 defeat at Sheffield United in his 18th game in charge. The 48-year-old is understood to be arriving in the UK on Tuesday to sign his contract and plans to bring three members of staff with him and hopes to be in the dugout for Wednesday's Championship fixture at home to Blackburn Rovers (19:45 GMT). Iordanescu guided Romania at Euro 2024 where they topped their group ahead of Belgium with all four sides ending level on four points from three games before a 3-0 defeat against the Netherlands in the Round of 16. Iordanescu - whose father Anghel had three spells in charge of the Romanian national team, leading them in two World Cups and two European Championships - left his last role at Polish club Legia Warsaw in October 2025. It was the 48-year-old's ninth club over a 15-year coaching career which has taken in Bulgarian club CSKA Sofia as well as Steaua Bucharest and Cluj among others in his homeland. Dionisi, who departed with the Hornets in 21st, four points above the relegation zone, was only appointed in June after the departure of Ed Still, who himself lasted only three months at Vicarage Road. Still, Javi Gracia and Paulo Pezzolano were all also given full-time contracts after Tom Cleverley left in May 2025. The 46-year-old Italian was Watford's 12th head coach, not including interim bosses, since the end of the 2020-21 season, and leaves the Hornets searching for a 25th since the Pozzo family took over the club in 2012. The club have had 57 permanent managers in their 145-year history. Pioneer or coach-eater? The complex world of Pozzo's Watford Watford sack boss Dionisi after 18 games Latest Watford news, analysis and fan views

item.title: PSG and Bayern Munich set for blockbuster transfer battle over Roma sensation Donyell Malen
item.description: AS Roma v ACF Fiorentina - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Paris Saint-Germain and Bayern Munich are preparing to battle for Roma sensation Donyell Malen in the January transfer window. The Dutch forward has been in devastating form in Serie A, prompting Europe's heavyweights to eye a massive winter move amid their respective injury crises. PSG and Bayern eye Malen PSG and Bayern are preparing to test Roma in the January transfer window. Both clubs have identified Malen as a priority attacking target for the winter market. The 27-year-old forward has been a revelation in Serie A this season. According to Calcio Mercato , his extraordinary form has attracted serious attention from the European heavyweights. Both clubs are desperate for immediate attacking reinforcements following severe injury blows. This has set the stage for a massive transfer battle in the upcoming window. Injury crises prompt transfer search The sudden interest in Malen is directly linked to major injury crises in Paris and Munich. The Parisians recently lost both Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue to significant long-term injuries. The Bavarians are dealing with an equally devastating situation. The German club will be without reigning Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane for several months due to a severe ankle injury. These absences mean Malen would be guaranteed immediate playing time at either club. A mid-season move could offer the Netherlands international the most lucrative contract of his career. Europe's most prolific forward Malen is currently enjoying the best spell of his professional career in the Italian capital. The former Borussia Dortmund attacker has registered an incredible 16 goals in just 15 appearances this season. This stunning return makes him the top scorer in Serie A. Following a recent four-goal haul against Parma, statistics show he is currently creating more chances than Kane did before his injury. item.title: Hearts v Celtic – Club make decision on our ticket allocation for Tynecastle
item.description: Hearts v Celtic – Club make decision on our ticket allocation for Tynecastle Celtic has today provided supporters with an update of the away ticket allocation for Sunday’s trip to Tynecastle after the Edinburgh side reduced our allocation yet again, this time by an additional 20%. 25th January 2026; Tynecastle, Scottish Premiership, Hearts versus Celtic; Turnstyles at Tynecastle. Photo Vagelis Georgariou Regardless of the reasons given you can’t help feeling that it’s petty, small minded and spiteful after Daizen Maeda and Callum Osmand swung the title in Celtic’s favour on the closing day of last season in what will remain an unforgettable afternoon at Paradise. The away allocation for our first visit to Tynecastle was recently reduced to just 508 tickets with many Celtic supporters who regularly travel to away matches believing that the club should REJECT the allocation in its entirety, meaning that there would also be no allocation for Hearts fans on their next visit to Celtic Park. 25th January 2026; Tynecastle Park, Edinburgh, Scotland: Scottish Premiership Football, Hearts versus Celtic Celtic has taken time to consider all views and opinions and has this lunchtime provided a clear summary of their deliberations, and their decision to go ahead and accept the tickets However any supporter who is successful in the resulting ballot but does NOT wish to added the game on Sunday out of principle will NOT have their away attendance record affected as a result. So fair play to Celtic on this one. They have listened to supporters. They have reached a decision which they have explained via the club’s official website and they have made provision for any Celtic supporters who if successful in the ballot would rather tell Hearts where to stuff their allocation that go to the game. Here’s the ticket allocation update from Celtic… ‘As supporters will know, our allocation for our forthcoming match against Heart of Midlothian at Tynecastle Stadium has been cut by 20%, compared to our previous visit. 25th January 2026; Tynecastle Park, Scottish Premiership Hearts versus Celtic; Celtic huddle There have been a variety of views expressed to the Club from supporters in relation to accepting this allocation. Some groups representing travelling supporters explained to the Club that their members did not wish to accept the tickets because of the reduced allocation. We have taken that into consideration and also raised their concerns with the home club, who have assured us that they have spoken to Police Scotland. Having carefully considered all of the circumstances, we can confirm we will accept the allocation of 508 tickets. Daizen Maeda of Celtic reacts after scoring his team’s second goal during the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Heart of Midlothian at Celtic Park on May 16, 2026. item.title: 'My silence should never be mistaken for weakness': Prithvi Shaw warns of legal action
item.description: NEW DELHI: Prithvi Shaw has hit back at former cricketer Yograj Singh over his remarks about the batter's career and personal life. Shaw said he had nothing to hide about his past but would not allow anyone to use it to spread negativity, damage his reputation or gain publicity. Yograj had blamed Shaw's career decline on his lifestyle, including partying, drinking and being in bad company. He also compared the Indian batter's situation with that of former India cricketer Vinod Kambli. "Why did Prithvi Shaw go downhill? It happened with Vinod Kambli before him. It was because of parties, womanising, cigarettes, and drinking. I once asked Kambli, ‘What are you, son?’ You have so much talent," Yograj said on Sports Launchpad. "You are coming to your room at 2.30 in the night. He said, ‘Your days are over, and we’re playing a different kind of cricket now.’ The next morning, Courtney Walsh bowled him, and India lost the match. Then the girl he was with left him, and no one offered him cigarettes and alcohol. The same happened with Shaw. When you go to parties, womanise, drink, and are in bad company, the same will happen to you as happened to them," he added. Shaw warns of legal action Shaw responded to Yograj's comments through a detailed Instagram statement. The batter said he had no issues with his past but would not accept attempts to target him or spread false claims about his personal life. "My past is a part of my life, and I have absolutely nothing to hide or be ashamed of. However, I will not tolerate individuals deliberately using my name, my personal life, or my past to spread negativity, create unnecessary controversy, damage my reputation, or gain publicity and attention at my expense. There is a clear difference between expressing an opinion and deliberately targeting someone with false, misleading, defamatory, or malicious content. Let this be a clear and final warning: Any individual or platform engaging in such activities may face appropriate legal action," Shaw said. The batter also said he was ready to take legal steps to protect his dignity, privacy and reputation. He made it clear that his silence should not be mistaken for weakness. "I reserve the right to pursue all legal remedies available to protect my dignity, privacy, and reputation. My silence should never be mistaken for weakness. I choose to move forward with dignity, but I will not hesitate to stand up for myself," he added. Shaw last represented India in 2021. The 27-year-old has played five Tests, six ODIs and one T20I for India.

item.title: Mendon's title hopes ends in state finals loss to Gaylord St. Mary
item.description: MARQUETTE — The Mendon Hornets have a love-hate relationship with the Superior Dome. Making it all the way north to play in the state finals is certainly an accomplishment. Mendon has done it twice now since moving to the 8-player football divisions of the MHSAA. Northern Michigan University is the host site for the 8-player finals and Mendon has now dropped both games it has played inside the Superior Dome. Despite doing a lot of positive things on Saturday, Mendon came up short in the state championship game. The Hornets faced off against a strong Gaylord St. Mary team and ultimately, the Snowbirds made big plays when it mattered and took advantage of some Mendon miscues. The end result was St. Mary's first state championship in football as the Snowbirds picked up a 49-34 victory in the Division 2, 8-player finals. "We just couldn't get out of our own way at times, we made some mistakes today we hadn't made all year," Mendon coach Bobby Kretschman said. "Sometimes that's gonna happen when you play a good team. I don't wanna take anything away from them. Our kids played hard. We battled the whole game and didn't quit. This was a hell of a lot more fun than when we were here in '22." item.content:encoded: MARQUETTE — The Mendon Hornets have a love-hate relationship with the Superior Dome. Making it all the way north to play in the state finals is certainly an accomplishment. Mendon has done it twice now since moving to the 8-player football divisions of the MHSAA. Northern Michigan University is the host site for the 8-player finals and Mendon has now dropped both games it has played inside the Superior Dome. Despite doing a lot of positive things on Saturday, Mendon came up short in the state championship game. The Hornets faced off against a strong Gaylord St. Mary team and ultimately, the Snowbirds made big plays when it mattered and took advantage of some Mendon miscues. The end result was St. Mary's first state championship in football as the Snowbirds picked up a 49-34 victory in the Division 2, 8-player finals. "We just couldn't get out of our own way at times, we made some mistakes today we hadn't made all year," Mendon coach Bobby Kretschman said. "Sometimes that's gonna happen when you play a good team. I don't wanna take anything away from them. Our kids played hard. We battled the whole game and didn't quit. This was a hell of a lot more fun than when we were here in '22." SUCCESS IN SNACKS: Sturgis couple finds success with Wagyu beef snacks GRIFFITH-MATHEWS READY TO RETIRE: As Leasa Griffith-Mathews says goodbye, she's proud of her time in Mendon Mendon's previous trip to the Superior Dome came in 2022, when the Hornets lost to Powers North Central 66-26. So for the second time in as many trips to Marquette, the Hornets claimed a trophy – but it was not the one they were in search of at the end of the season. "I'm proud of the kids. I'm proud of everything we accomplished," Kretschman said. "We just fell short today." Both teams came into the contest with records of 12-0 for the year. The Hornets made their way to the finals largely in part to running over everyone in their path. Running the football has always been a staple of Mendon football and this year proved to be more of the same. But St. Mary made big play after big play when it counted. St. Mary led the game 35-34 with just under five minutes remaining in the contest. To get the deficit down to a point, the Hornets scored for the final time on a 4-yard TD rush from Logan Stuart which capped off an 18-play, 80-yard drive for the Hornets which took 7:30 off the clock. St. Mary would answer with the final two touchdowns of the game. They both came from Cal Royce, who had a monster game on both sides of the football. He scored on runs of 27 and 39 yards in the final five minutes of the contest to give the Snowbirds the lead and eventually put the game out of reach. "That QB was an absolute stud," Kretschman said of Royce. "We had him wrapped up at times and he still made some big plays." Mendon started the game on the opening drive and took half the opening quarter. The Hornets were methodical and marched it down the field, but eventually turned it over on downs. After St. Mary got the football, the Snowbirds had a limited drive themselves and punted it back to Mendon. "That whole first half, we played the way we wanted to play it," Kretschman said. "Honestly, after the first quarter, we felt alright. We were keeping our seals, moved the ball. That first drive was our style of football." Mendon first scored midway through the second for the opening points of the game. Xavior Zinsmaster found the end zone on a 1-yard TD plunge which ended a 12-play, 36-yard drive. The Hornets missed the conversion attempt but led 6-0. On the ensuing possession, Royce found Joe Jacobson for a big pass play, covering 70 yards and a touchdown. The extra point gave St. Mary a 7-6 edge. Royce scored his first TD with under two minutes until halftime. It was a 73-yard scamper to the end zone. He would also kick a field goal as time expired in the opening half, an 18-yarder. Prior to the field goal, Mendon got a TD from Zinsmaster on a 2-yard run. The Snowbirds led 16-12 at the break. They scored first in the second half as well on a 50-yard TD pass from Royce to Cash Wcisel. Mendon's next two possessions each ended in touchdowns as well. The Snowbirds led the game 23-12, but Mendon put up the next 14 points. Zak Iobe scored on a 24-yard TD pass from Owen Klinger for the first of the two. Then, Zinsmaster scored his third TD of the game on a 2-yard TD run to make it 26-23 Hornets. Following that, St. Mary scored four times in the final quarter and a half. "We just couldn't catch a break, couple turnovers. We capitalized on some things, but little things we hadn't done all year hurt us," Kretschman said. "It's a game of inches and they took advantage when they had to." Mendon ran an astounding 86 plays from scrimmage when it had the football. It covered 388 total yards. The Snowbirds totaled 463 yards on just 30 snaps, averaging better than 23 yards per offensive play. In terms of time of possession, Mendon was right where it wanted to be with a 36:31 - 11:29 advantage. But the big plays by St. Mary proved to be the difference. Mendon sustained its drives and reached the red zone seven times in the contest, cashing in on five of those drives for points. Zinsmaster led Mendon with 159 yards on the ground in the game, he scored three times. Iobe ran for 87 yards and Stuart added 68 with a score. Klinger made six completions covering 73 yards and the TD to Iobe. Iobe hauled in three catches for 43, Zinsmaster caught two for eight and Aron Wendt caught one pass for 22 yards. Defensively, Mendon was led by Conner Doehring, Tristin Wood and Zinsmaster all with four stops. Royce finished with an impressive game. He ran for 199 and three scores. He threw for 252 yards and four TDs. He also led the defense with 13 tackles and forced a Mendon fumble down on the goal line, when the Hornets were heading into the end zone. The fumble went out of bounds inside the end zone and resulted in a touchback for the Snowbirds. St. Mary ended its season with the school's first football title and a 13-0 record. Mendon said goodbye to its seniors and ended 12-1. Kretschman said the tradition of Mendon football will continue as the Hornets look to re-tool for next season. Contact Sports Editor Brandon Watson at bwatson@gannett.com . Follow him on X, formerly known as Twitter, @BwatsonSJ. item.description: Feast Week is here! The Wildcats took a two-point lead into the break after a 22-point first half from Milan Momcilovic. The Hoosiers made the right adjustments at halftime, holding Momcilovic to just six points in the second frame. Indiana's biggest advantage came at the free throw line, where they went 28-for-31 (90%) compared to Kentucky's 3-for-7 (42%). Indiana was fouled on a three-point attempt four different times during the game. Bryce Lindsay, who led the Hoosiers with 20 points, had a hilarious interaction with Jon Rothstein in his post-game interview. More Friday scores to know: Seton Hall 87 - NC State 81 (OT) : Seton Hall took home the Baha Mar Championship in an overtime thriller. Terry Copeland earned Tournament MVP after with 22 points and nine rebounds in the title game. Rodney Brown Jr. added 24 points for Seton Hall, who is now 5-1 on the season. Ven-Allen Lubin had 27 points and eight rebounds for NC State. Murray State 70 - Wisconsin 53 : The Racers took home the consolation game at Baha Mar thanks to a 26-point performance from Roman Domon. Wisconsin was held to just 5-for-25 shooting from three and turned the ball over 17 times. Murray State led by 16 at the half and it never got closer than eight points the rest of the way. Georgia 88 - Georgia Tech 82 : Georgia opened the game on a 12-0 run and never trailed. Kanon Catchings had 19 points and nine rebounds. He was one of five Bulldogs in double figures. Tylis Jordan and Colby Garland each had 19 points for Georgia Tech. Minnesota 85 - Oklahoma State 70 : Kyan Evans opened the Charleston Classic with 15 points and 10 assists to be Oklahoma State. Isaac Asuma added 15 points and seven rebounds for the Gophers. Kashie Natt led the Cowboys with 22 points and nine rebounds. Iowa 83 - Xavier 65 : Isaia Howard and Trevin Jirak combined for 45 points as Iowa shot 60% (33-55) from the field to hand Xavier its first loss of the season. Mike Nwoko led the Musketeers with 21 points and seven rebounds. Campbell 80 - Kansas State 70 : Lance Waddles and Rashawn Inglemon each had 23 points for the Camels, handing Kansas State its second buy-game loss of the season. Brock Vice had 15 points and 10 rebounds for the Wildcats. Saint Mary's 95 - Saint Louis 78 : Saint Mary's made a staggering 37-of-38 free throw attempts, which proved to be the difference in their win over Saint Louis. item.title: Canadiens Make A 2nd Trade After Acquiring Dylan Larkin!
item.description: Canadiens Make A 2nd Trade After Acquiring Dylan Larkin! The Montreal Canadiens pulled off what will likely go down as the biggest trade of the 2026-27 National Hockey League regular season on Sunday night when they acquired former Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin in a blockbuster deal. It seems, however, that the Canadiens aren't done just yet, and if anything, they might be laying the groundwork for yet another big move before this season is all said and done. On Sunday night, they did so by pulling off yet another trade following the Larkin deal, this time with the Anaheim Ducks. In a weird little twist, the Red Wings were also sort of involved in this second trade, with their draft picks being the only assets exchanged between the Ducks and the Canadiens. Canadiens acquire: 2027 second-round draft pick (Red Wings) Ducks acquire: 2028 second-round draft pick (Red Wings) Given how much the Canadiens gave up in the Larkin deal, it seems they are all-in on the next few years being their championship window, and I suspect the pick they've just acquired from the Ducks might not remain in Montreal for very long. It's been a very busy time for Canadiens general manager Kent Hughes, but he is being rewarded for his hard work with praise from what sounds like a very happy Canadiens fan base.

item.title: Little solace - and no Solis - in setback at Stoke
item.description: [BBC] [Press Association] Did the international break come at the wrong time for us? We'd gone into it buoyant after our last-minute victory over Swansea, but we seemed to have lost momentum by the time we got to the Bet365 Stadium on Saturday afternoon. Although August Priske and James Beadle were back from injury, the big miss for me was Jhon Solis. When he isn't available, it makes a significant difference to the way we play. While Paik Seung-ho and Tomoki Iwata in midfield were the go-to pairing during our season in League One, they don't seem to provide enough physical presence in the Championship. In general, Blues were pretty lacklustre; we seemed a bit ring-rusty and while we managed to deal with Stoke's press in the first half, it didn't seem to leave us with much energy for attacking. This extended to us being caught out early in the second half and conceding. Although Chris Davies used most of the attacking options we had on the subs' bench, we just weren't clinical enough to force an equaliser, despite pushing Stoke hard towards the end of the game. Mark Robins is an experienced manager and a wily campaigner, and he had clearly set Stoke up to frustrate our attacking options. Even with Stoke down to 10 men in the second half, he bolstered his defence to hold on to their slender lead. This meeting with Stoke was always likely to be close; we were only separated by goal difference. To be honest, I'd have been happy with a point, but we couldn't find our way to one. However, we're still fourth and need to pick ourselves up ready for a trip to Burnley on Wednesday night. Hopefully, we will have sorted ourselves out by then. It's getting to that time where we need to start thinking about the transfer window again. Given that Marvin Ducksch is likely to be off, does our recruitment team need to think about another strong midfielder to go alongside Solis? item.title: Former top referee Dermot Gallagher rules on controversial Newcastle United v Arsenal incidents
item.description: Malick Thiaw goal celebration Newcastle against Arsenal Dermot Gallagher reviews controversial decisions in the Premier League after each round of games, on behalf of Sky Sports . The former top referee has now given his call on these incidents in the Newcastle United v Arsenal match. Dermot Gallagher looking at what happened during key moments in this match at St James’ Park . The two key moments both occurring during the second half. So what about these ‘controversial’ incidents… Dermot Gallagher talking to Sky Sports about these Newcastle United v Arsenal controversial incidents: INCIDENT: Harvey Barnes equalised for Newcastle against Arsenal following an error from Martin Odegaard, who was caught by Joe Willock after making the mistake. DERMOT GALLAGHER: “Calafiori is closest to him and he doesn’t think it’s a foul. He is chasing the ball.” FORMER PLAYER TIM SHERWOOD: “Very shocked if it had been ruled out. Nothing wrong with that.” FORMER PLAYER JAY BOTHROYD: “No problems at all. I thought, knowing his quality, I thought he would chest it down. You cannot give a foul for that. It is so soft.” INCIDENT: Joe Willock, Gabriel and David Raya bundle over inside the penalty area as Malick Thiaw pokes Newcastle United ahead. DERMOT GALLAGHER: “If you look, Gabriel has pinned Willock himself. It’s Gabriel who just falls into Raya.” JAY BOTHROYD: “I can’t argue with that, it’s the correct decision. If you’re giving fouls for that, it would be disgraceful.” TIM SHERWOOD: “Great decision. Willock knows what he’s doing.” In reality, I don’t think there was anything ‘controversial’ about either incident. There would have been if either goal had been disallowed! As Dermot Gallagher and his mates all say, nothing wrong with either United goal.

item.title: “Very Much Worried,” “Withdraw ASAP” – Carlos Alcaraz Fans Alarmed After ATP Finals Champ Heads to Davis Cup Despite Injury Scare
item.description: Mar 3, 2026; Indian Wells, CA, USA; Carlos Alcaraz (ESP) speaks to the media at a news conference during the BNP Paribas Open at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden. © Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Carlos Alcaraz faced criticism from fans for choosing to compete in the Davis Cup immediately after winning his maiden ATP Finals title, which marked a demanding run. Alcaraz won his first ATP Finals title after going unbeaten and defeating Alexander Zverev in the final. He also suffered an injury scare during his face-off with Daniil Medvedev in the group stage. He sustained a minor left hamstring issue early in the second set and played with his left thigh heavily strapped. Alcaraz will return to the court at the upcoming Davis Cup, which will be held from November 24-29 at the SuperTennis Arena (BolognaFiere) in Bologna, Italy. The Spaniard is reported to travel from Turin to Bologna by car on Monday, Nov. 23, after winning his first ATP Finals title on Sunday. He will be joined by his coach, Samu López, in the 331-km journey. Alcaraz’s decision sparked concern among tennis fans, one of whom expressed their concern and wrote: “Now I’m very much worried for his preseason if he plays next week and that hamstring keeps getting worse. Lord, protect this boy 🙏🏾” Another urged Alcaraz to withdraw from competing and focus on the upcoming season and added: “Withdraw asap man… focus on 2027” Another fan hoped for Alcaraz’s well-being and chimed in: Here are a few more reactions: Carlos Alcaraz makes his feelings known after winning his maiden ATP Finals title Carlos Alcaraz won the first ATP Finals title of his career with an unbeaten campaign. After defeating Alexander Zverev in the final in Turin on Sunday, he spoke about the physical setbacks and emotional demands he navigated during the run. In the press conference after his victory, Alcaraz said that winning his maiden ATP Finals title was a very special moment for him and his team. He reflected on his hard work and expressed his gratitude towards his team and family. “This one is special,” Alcaraz said. “This one means the world to me, to my team, to my family. They know how hard I’ve been chasing this moment, this trophy, this tournament, how hard I’ve been working for this tournament, to lift this trophy. So finally, to be able to lift the trophy here, it’s something amazing, the feeling that I have right now. It’s difficult to put into words, to be honest. So I’m really proud of everything I’ve done this week, with my team, with my close people, that without them, it wouldn’t be possible to lift this trophy.” “It is a tournament that I really wanted to win. I was chasing that moment really bad since a really long time. Once I got it, a lot of emotions came to me, came to my team. I was looking at them. They were screaming, they were celebrating, they were everything.” After the win in Turin, Carlos Alcaraz joined the list of players who have won all four majors and the Finals.
