item.content:encoded: Yahoo Sports AM is our daily newsletter that keeps you up to date on all things sports. Sign up here to get it every weekday morning. 🚨 HEADLINES 🏒 NHL blockbuster: The Red Wings are sending franchise mainstay Dylan Larkin to the Canadiens in a blockbuster deal that includes four players and six draft picks. The mega-trade ends a months-long saga in Detroit that began when Larkin requested a trade over the summer and saw his captaincy stripped. 🏎️ Verstappen takes Vegas: Red Bull's Max Verstappen won a wild race on Saturday night in Sin City, taking the Las Vegas Grand Prix for the third time in four years. McLaren's duo of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri filled out the podium. 🏀 50-point outbursts: James Harden (Cavaliers) scored 51 points on Friday, becoming the fourth-oldest NBA player to put up 50 in a game. A day later, Tyler Herro (Bucks) scored a career-high 50 points and Victor Wembanyama (Spurs) had his second 50-point game of the season . ⚽️ Favorites on the brink: Defending MLS Cup champion Inter Miami and top-seeded Nashville are both one loss away from a Round One exit after falling to Columbus and Cincinnati in their best-of-three series openers. Elsewhere: New England ( over Philadelphia ), Dallas ( over Portland ), Charlotte ( over Chicago ) and Vancouver ( over Salt Lake ) took 1-0 leads. 🏈 FCS bracket revealed: Defending champion Montana State earned the No. 1 seed in the 24-team FCS playoff bracket , while undefeated Tarleton State had to settle for the No. 2 seed. The top eight seeds all receive a first-round bye, with play beginning this weekend. See what else is trending on Yahoo Sports . ⚾️ METS SIGN SKUBAL TO HISTORIC DEAL (Ethan Palowitz/Yahoo Sports) After half a season with the Dodgers, two-time Cy Young Award winner Tarik Skubal has agreed to sign a nine-year, $450 million deal with the Mets , the largest contract ever given to a pitcher (by a lot). Behind the scenes: Skubal reportedly met with four teams in person last week: the Mets, Blue Jays, Padres and Dodgers. He chose New York, which will award him a $45 million bonus at signing, essentially giving the 30-year-old southpaw a full season of pay ahead of the projected Dec. 1 lockout. Jordan Shusterman, Yahoo Sports: Two years ago, as the baseball industry descended upon Dallas for the annual winter meetings, news broke of a truly jaw-dropping free-agent agreement: The Mets had signed outfielder Juan Soto to a 15-year deal worth $765 million, the largest contract in North American professional sports history. It was the result of a generational talent hitting the open market at an unusually young age, a super-agent in Scott Boras fetching an unthinkable sum in free agency and an outrageously wealthy owner in Steve Cohen willing to bid as high as necessary to get the deal done. Well, here we are again. That seismic Soto contract set the stage for another lucrative link-up between Boras and Cohen two years later. This time, Boras' top client couldn't wait for the winter meetings. With a work stoppage looming, it became apparent early this offseason that Skubal's free agency would be expedited. Across the league, the ramifications of Skubal's record-smashing contract could be significant in the short and long term. His agreement being finalized well before Dec. 1 could open the door for a flurry of activity, as pitching-needy clubs — whether or not they were chasing Skubal — can now pivot to other arms in free agency or trade. Then there's the matter of how Skubal's gigantic contract and the Mets' lavish spending fit into the larger conversation about baseball's economic system, which is about to be the subject of intense negotiations over the next several months. And for the Mets, the signing of Skubal accomplishes their No. 1 offseason objective, but their to-do list is far from complete as they seek to rebound from a dismal, 74-win season. If anything, this deal refocuses the hot stove spotlight on president of baseball operations David Stearns, whose team-building strategies executed alongside owner Steve Cohen's exorbitant spending have thus far fallen short of expectations. Keep reading: Signing Skubal is a loud reminder of the Mets' financial might and an expensive step back toward contention 🏈 HOME TEAMS STRIKE BACK Chuba Hubbard's first of two touchdowns on the day. (Grant Halverson/Getty Images) We wrote last week about the NFL's disappearing home-field advantage. Naturally, every home team went out and won on Sunday… except for the Chargers , who fell to the Jets in Los Angeles. Panthers 35, Ravens 33: Carolina seized control of the NFC South after outlasting Baltimore in a back-and-forth contest that featured seven lead changes and 799 yards of offense. Cowboys 51, Titans 30: Scorigami alert! This rout produced the 1,101st unique final score in NFL history and marked the second straight week that Dallas was involved in one (46-40). Eagles 19, Steelers 16: Even the Birds, losers of seven straight, got the job done at home. Maybe we should have seen it coming: The Steelers haven't won in Philadelphia since 1965 . Giants 23, Jaguars 18: Big Blue held on for the win in the day's only matchup between first-place teams. Jags fans aren't happy about a late controversial call: Should this have been ruled a TD? Lions 31, Buccaneers 21: Detroit won its sixth straight game behind Jahmyr Gibbs, who had his 18th career multi-TD performance. That's tied for the most ever through four seasons. Bills 26, Dolphins 9: Buffalo cruised to its sixth straight victory behind a defense that has gone 43 consecutive drives without allowing a TD, a streak that dates all the way back to Nov. 1. Broncos 38, Raiders 24: Denver also won its sixth straight game, leaning on rookie Jonah Coleman (24 car, 111 yds, 3 TD) to spoil the best start of rookie Fernando Mendoza's young career (267 yards, 3 TD, INT). Bears 21, Saints 13: Da Bears are 5-0 since Caleb Williams returned from injury, and they haven't trailed once during that span. The last time Chicago had such a streak? 1959. Chiefs 34, Cardinals 7: Travis Kelce caught his 109th and 110th career TDs, moving him past Rob Gronkowski (108) for third-most among tight ends. Only Antonio Gates (118) and Tony Gonzalez (115) have more. (Agustin Cuevas/Getty Images) 🇲🇽 Meanwhile, in Mexico City: The 49ers steamrolled the Vikings, 35-10 , in the ninth and final international game of the season to join the Bills at an NFL-best 9-1. Minnesota's vaunted defense was no match for Kyle Shanahan's game plan and Brock Purdy's arm (21/26, 255 yds, 3 TD). Further reading: Brock Purdy, MVP? 49ers, Super Bowl champions? It's all on the table now for San Francisco 🏆 IN PHOTOS: CHAMPIONS CROWNED (Patrick Smith/NWSL via Getty Images) ⚽️ Washington, D.C. — The Kansas City Current beat the Washington Spirit, 2-1, on Saturday to capture their first NWSL championship in their sixth season as a franchise. It was a familiar heartbreak for the Spirit, who have now lost three straight title games, all by one goal. Sensing a theme? The Current join the Valkyries, Brewers and Indiana football as first-time champions crowned in 2026. That's to say nothing of the Knicks (first title in 53 years), Hurricanes (20 years) and Seahawks (12 years). (Clive Brunskill/Getty Images) 🎾 Turin, Italy — Carlos Alcaraz took down Alexander Zverev in straight sets on Sunday to win the ATP Finals, joining Roger Federer, Novak Djokovic and Andre Agassi as the only men to win all four Grand Slams and the tour's season-ending event. At 23, he's by far the youngest to do so. Man on fire: Alcaraz has been on a heater since returning from a wrist injury in August, going 25-2 overall and winning four of his past five events. He now owns 12 of the 15 most important trophies in tennis, with only Shanghai, Canada and an Olympic gold medal missing from his collection. Threepeat! (Julio Aguilar/Getty Images) ⛳️ Naples, Florida — Thailand's Jeeno Thitikul (-24) fired a 7-under 65

item.title: ‘Take Some Accountability,’ This Guy Needs To Take a Hike’ — Steelers Fans Push Back on Aaron Rodgers’ Reported Complaint on Team Meetings
item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) in the tunnel before game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field. (Eric Hartline-Imagn Images) The Pittsburgh Steelers have plenty to sort through in the film room this week, and Aaron Rodgers has thoughts on how that room ought to run. During the CBS broadcast of Sunday’s 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles, reporter Melanie Collins relayed that the veteran quarterback wants more interaction when the team gathers for meetings. “He called for more interaction. He said it’s tough nowadays with these iPads,” Collins said. However, the request didn’t sit well with some fans, who turned the talk of accountability back on the quarterback. Melanie Collins Details Aaron Rodgers’ Point About iPads in Team Meetings The remarks came on a rough afternoon for Pittsburgh. The Steelers dropped to 6-4 with their second straight loss, a week after falling 38-18 in Cincinnati, and Rodgers was sacked five times while the offense converted 5 of 17 third downs. Collins kept going and gave her own read on the quarterback’s tone along the way. “Back in the day, you could check guys’ notes and make sure they were writing things down. It almost felt like he was calling out the guys a little bit for a lack of details. He wants everyone to feel like they’re contributing to what’s happening on game day, even when they’re not on the field.” Some fans decided to turn that call for details back on the quarterback himself. “Dude was overthrowing by a mile. Take some accountability bro,” one said , while another added , “The guy who screams at WRs when he throws it 10 yards over their heads wants more accountability? That’s rich.” Rodgers completed 30 of 44 passes, a 68.2% clip, for 227 yards and a touchdown without an interception Sunday, and his completion percentage over expected of 2.2 ranked 10th of 24 qualified quarterbacks in Week 11. For the season, though, his 60.9% completion rate through Week 11 sits 23rd of 32 qualified quarterbacks, and his 86.6 passer rating is tied for 19th of 32. Pro Football Network’s NFL QB Impact Grade has him at 67 over the same span, 29th of 33 graded quarterbacks. Rodgers Points to the Run Game After Week 11 Loss to Eagles Rodgers pointed to the running game after the loss, where Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle combined for 43 yards on 14 carries. “We’d like to run the ball. That makes everything easier. We weren’t running very well. They’ve got a good defense … We knew it was going to be a challenge, but we had plenty of opportunities. (Our) defense played really well, especially after the first couple drives, and we got to win games like that.” “Maybe Rodgers needs to take some responsibility for this debacle? That’s rich.” Rodgers completed 30 of 44 passes, a 68.2% clip, for 227 yards and a touchdown without an interception Sunday, and his completion percentage over expected of 2.2 ranked 10th of 24 qualified quarterbacks in Week 11. For the season, though, his 60.9% completion rate through Week 11 sits 23rd of 32 qualified quarterbacks, and his 86.6 passer rating is tied for 19th of 32. Nah, blame the iPads,” one fan remarked. Another fan wanted the quarterback’s own tape brought into the meeting-room conversation. “Has he watched video of his own play? This guy needs to take a hike.” Not every response focused on the quarterback’s arm, and one came from a familiar name in Pittsburgh. Trai Essex, a two-time Super Bowl champion with the Steelers, took notice of Collins’ report, saying, “Need some thumb pointers. Tired of hearing about everybody else. It’s Week 11 and we are using the media to send messages about how team meetings are ran. The passive-aggressiveness and code words in pressers is maddening.” Pittsburgh won’t have long to hash any of it out. The Steelers are third in the AFC North at 6-4, and they host the 8-2 Denver Broncos, who sit first in the AFC West, at Acrisure Stadium on Friday for a 3 p.m. ET kickoff in Week 12. That gives the Steelers a short Thanksgiving week to get everyone on the same page. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

item.title: Napoli visit Man City without 11 players as Vergara faces lengthy layoff
item.description: Napoli visit Man City without 11 players as Vergara faces lengthy layoff Napoli will travel to Manchester City without 11 players, including four centre-backs, while Antonio Vergara is expected to be sidelined for more than two months with a high-grade tear in his left thigh. Napoli face several selection problems ahead of Tuesday’s Champions League away match against Manchester City. The Partenopei, who sit eighth in Serie A, will travel to England without 11 first-team players. NAPLES, ITALY – OCTOBER 20: Massimiliano Allegri, Manager of SSC Napoli, reacts during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between SSC Napoli and FK Bodo/Glimt at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on October 20, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) Alisson Santos, Benoit Badiashile, Alessandro Buongiorno, captain Giovanni Di Lorenzo, Stanislav Lobotka, Alex Meret and David Neres are injured; Rafa Marin is suspended, while Luca Marianucci and Costantino Favasuli are not part of their UEFA squad. Vergara was the latest player to suffer an injury, coming off in the first half of Saturday’s 1-0 win over Torino at the Stadio Maradona. Napoli issued a statement on Monday after the Italy international underwent medical tests. The club said Vergara had suffered a high-grade tear of the right biceps femoris muscle in his left thigh. According to Sky Sport, the 23-year-old is expected to be out for more than two months. NAPLES, ITALY – NOVEMBER 21: Antonio Vergara of SSC Napoli is consoled by teammate Matteo Politano as he is substituted off after sustaining an injury during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and Torino FC at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on November 21, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) Napoli’s injury crisis has hit hardest in attack and defence. In Manchester, coach Massimiliano Allegri will be without four of his six centre-backs, predictably prompting Mathias Olivera to join Amir Rrahmani and Sam Beukema in a three-man back line. Allegri will hold a pre-match press conference in Manchester later today, alongside former Manchester City star Kevin De Bruyne. NAPLES, ITALY – NOVEMBER 21: Kevin De Bruyne of SSC Napoli is challenged by Rafik Belghali of Torino FC during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and Torino FC at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on November 21, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) Allegri has already suggested Napoli may not travel to Manchester with their highest motivation. “It’s a very important match and a great one to play in,” the coach said after Saturday’s win over Torino. “We have to be realistic; our Champions League campaign will be decided against Club Brugge, Sabah and Viking. We had to beat Bodo, and we did. Tuesday will be very important and difficult, but we need to sort out the league, and the home match against Club Brugge will be crucial.”

item.title: Marseille manager Bruno Genesio: ‘There is a global phenomenon of fragility as soon as we concede a goal.’
item.description: Marseille manager Bruno Genesio: ‘There is a global phenomenon of fragility as soon as we concede a goal.’ Olympique de Marseille were seemingly in complete control and sauntering towards a victory against Le Mans FC that would have extended their winning run in Ligue 1 to six games. 2-0 up thanks to goals from Amine Gouiri and Igor Paixao, Bruno Genesio’s side were cruising until Louis Mafouta’s direct free-kick, which struck the inside of the post before going in on the 70th minute. That goal instigated a collapse from Marseille. Mafouta then missed a penalty to level the scores, but it was a miss that would ultimately prove inconsequential, with Le Mans securing a spectacular comeback win thanks to Jean Vercruysse’s 95th-minute winner at the Vélodrome. “There is a global phenomenon of fragility as soon as we concede a goal,” reacted Genesio in a post-match press conference attended by Get French Football News. “There are also tactical problems to solve because we are poorly positioned on the goals that we concede […] there are also mental problems that are present sometimes at the ends of matches. Tonight, we were at 100% for 60% of the match and then we were below 100% for 40% of it.” GFFN | Luke Entwistle

item.title: Bayern Munich could lose out to Bayer Leverkusen in race for Wael Mohya
item.description: 06 November 2026, Hamburg: Soccer, Men's, Bundesliga, Hamburger SV vs. Borussia Mönchengladbach, Matchday 9 at the Volksparkstadion. Wael Mohya (Borussia Mönchengladbach) reacts. Photo: Marcus Brandt/dpa - IMPORTANT NOTICE: In accordance with the regulations of the Bundesliga and the DFB (German Football Association), it is prohibited to use or allow the use of photographs taken in the stadium and/or during the game in the form of sequential images and/or video-like photo series. (Photo by Marcus Brandt/picture alliance via Getty Images) Bayern Munich could face an increasingly difficult battle to sign Borussia Mönchengladbach prospect Wael Mohya, as Bayer Leverkusen looks to get ahead of the competition. According to a report from Bild (via @iMiaSanMia ), Leverkusen has stepped up its pursuit of the 16-year-old attacking talent. The club has already contacted Mohya’s agent, Thies Bliemeister, and plans to speak with the player, his family, and Gladbach about a potential move. Leverkusen has made a point of signing some of Germany’s brightest young prospects in recent years, having landed Ibrahim Maza in 2025 and Kennet Eichhorn in 2026. Mohya could be the next name on that list. Bayern’s interest remains appealing to Mohya, and the youngster is reportedly not intimidated by the prospect of competing for playing time in Munich. However, Gladbach’s prec arious sporting situation could make a transfer more attainable for interested clubs. The report puts a realistic asking price at around €20 million, al though Gladbach will attempt to negotiate a higher fee. That valuation could change depending on the club’s Bundesliga standing and the threat of relegation. A decision on Mohya’s future is expected around Christmas. Bayern will need to make its intentions clear if it wants to prevent Leverkusen from winning the race for another highly rated Bundesliga youngster. Join the conversation! item.title: Lions vs. Bears odds: Detroit home underdogs on Thanksgiving
item.description: Detroit Lions safety Brian Branch (32) sacks Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams (18) during the second half at Ford Field in Detroit on Sunday, Sept. 14, 2025. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co As the Detroit Lions enter Thanksgiving week, they’ve won six straight games, are 8-2 overall, and are 2-0 in the division, sitting in first place in the NFC North . This Thursday, they’ll host the Chicago Bears, who also enter this game at 8-2, but are 0-2 in the division, putting them in second place. Despite the Lions’ better record and the game being at Ford Field in downtown Detroit, the folks over at FanDuel Sportsbook have set the opening betting line at Lions +2.5 points . In Ben Johnson’s first year as head coach, the Bears went 11-6 and won the NFC North. They beat the Packers in the Wild Card but lost to the Rams in the Divisional round, ending a season that exceeded expectations. This offseason, the Bears made a few tweaks to their offense while overhauling half of their defense. On offense, priority No. 1 was replacing their center, Drew Dalman, who surprisingly retired. So the Bears traded with the Patriots for Garrett Bradbury, then drafted Iowa’s Logan Jones in the second round. At receiver, they traded away DJ Moore and replaced him with former Lion Kalif Raymond, who has stepped into a starting role in the slot and flashed. On defense, the Bears lost all four of their top safeties (Kevin Byard, Jaquan Brisker, Jonathan Owens, and Chauncey Gardner-Johnson), their top linebacker in Tremaine Edmunds, starting NT Andrew Billings, and EDGE Dominique Robinson. At safety, the Bears made two splash moves: drafting Dillon Thieneman in the first round and signing Coby Bryant in free agency, who unfortunately suffered a season-ending injury, but they also signed Cam Lewis, who has since stepped into a starting role. Former Michigan Wolverine Devin Bush was signed in free agency to fill an Edmunds-sized void at linebacker, and Neville Gallimore was brought in to start at nose tackle. When Gallimore struggled, Chicago made a significant in-season trade, sending two first-round picks to acquire NT Jeffery Simmons. The Bears opened the season by dropping 59 points on the Panthers and had Johnson talking about setting the NFL scoring record . The next week, the Bears scored only three points in a 9-3 loss to the Vikings. Wins over the Eagles and Jets helped them regain rhythm, but they fell to the Packers in Week 5—their third consecutive loss to an NFC North rival dating back to last season when they lost to the Lions in Week 18. Since their 3-2 start to the season, the Bears have been on a roll, winning their last five games, rolling up over 30 points on the Falcons (31-23), Patriots (30-24), and Seahawks (34-17), but they have shown some kinks in the armor of late. item.title: Michigan State vs Arkansas Preview
item.description: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 17: Head coach John Calipari of the Arkansas Razorbacks looks on during the first half against the Indiana Hoosiers in the Bad Boy Mowers Series at Madison Square Garden on November 17, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images Michigan State basketball has just one game this week, as the Spartans head to Little Caesar’s Arena in Detroit to take on the Arkansas Razorbacks on Thanksgiving Day (4:30 PM ET, CBS). The game should tip shortly after the conclusion of the Detroit Lions – Chicago Bears game across the street at Ford Field (1 PM ET, also on CBS). Here is a closer look at Arkansas, MSU’s Turkey Day opponent. Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: Improved notifications system! Fewer ads Create community posts Comment on articles, community posts Rec comments, community posts Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Season Recap Arkansas came into the season with high expectations but, perhaps like MSU, have experienced some ups and downs in the season’s early going. The Razorbacks sit at 4-2 with wins ranging from relatively easy outings to total blowouts against Arkansas-Pine Bluff, Robert Morris, Central Arkansas, and Mississippi Valley State. Each of these wins were at home. The two losses were neutral site games against stronger competition. Arkansas fell 91-72 to #9 Virginia on November 8 in a game played in Washington, DC. The second loss came on November 17 in Madison Square Garden, as Indiana knocked off Arkansas 81-76. Expected Starters Part of Arkansas’ struggles may revolve around figuring how to combine one talented returning veteran with several highly-ranked freshman and a couple of transfers. Here is an interesting article from Nolan Dobson from Roundtable Sports – Arkansas that discusses Arkansas’ roster construction this year. Billy Richmond III is the only player in the Arkansas rotation that returns from last year’s team. The Hogs’ other starters include a freshman big man with Finnish National Team experience, two transfers, and 5-star freshman. The stats below for each player represent their averages and shot totals in Arkansas’ games against their top competition so far this season – Virginia and Indiana. These are not their season averages through six games. #3 Miikka Muurinen . 7-0, 220, FR, F. From Finland, where he has played on the national team. Helped Finland to a fourth-place finish at the 2025 FIBA EuroBasket Championship. This year against Virginia & Indiana: 20 MIN, 11 PTS, 5-11 FG, 3-8 3FG, 3 REB, 1 AST, 2.5 TO. #21 Cooper Bowser . 6-11, 230, SR, F. Transfer from Furman, where he averaged 13.8 points and 5.9 rebounds per game last season. Against UVA & IU: 22.5 MIN, 4.5 PTS, 4-7 FG (no 3-point attempts), 4.5 REB, 3 AST. #5 Jeremiah Wilkinson . 6-1, 190, JR. G. Began career at Cal; transferred to Arkansas from Georgia, where he averaged 17.4 PPG last season. Against UVA & IU: 17 MIN, 6.5 PTS, 5-14 FG, 3-8 3FG, 0 REBS, 0

Against UVA & IU: 17 MIN, 6.5 PTS, 5-14 FG, 3-8 3FG, 0 REBS, 0.5 AST, 1 TO. #23 Jordan Smith Jr . 6-2, 210, FR, G. 5-star recruit, ranked the #2 overall recruit and #1 combo guard in the 2026 class by 247Sports, ESPN, and On3. Against UVA & IU: 31 MIN, 15.5 PTS, 12-28 FG, 1-3 3FG, 2 REBS, 2.5 AST, 2 TO. #24 Billy Richmond III . 6-7, 205, JR, G. Started 19 of 37 games for Arkansas last year, averaged 11.2 PPG on 56.3% shooting. Against UVA & IU: 31.5 MIN, 13.5 PTS, 8-14 FG, 2-5 3FG, 7 REBS, 3.5 AST, o.5 TO. Off the Bench So far this year, the Razorbacks have brought four very talented freshmen off the bench. Davion Thomas, a 4-star recruit out of Link Academy in Missouri, saw the most run off the bench in Arkansas’ games against Virginia and Indiana. #1 Abdou Toure . 6-5, 215, FR, F. 5-star and consensus top-15 recruit in the 2026 class. Against UVA & IU: 12.5 MIN, 7 PTS, 6-11 FG, 1-4 3FG, 2.5 REB. #7 JJ Andrews . 6-6, 235, FR, F. 5-star recruit with national ranking among the various services ranging from #12 to #22. Against UVA & IU: 19.5 MIN, 3 PTS, 2-9 FG, 1-4 3 FG, 4.5 REB, 1 TO. #8 Maper Maker . 7-0, 215, FR, F. From Australia, where he played in 2025-2026. Previous prep experience at Bella Vista College Prep and Dream City Christian (both in Arizona). Only played 1 minute against Indiana. Against Virginia: 22 MIN, 0 PTS, 0-2 FG, 4 REB, 3 TO. #9 Davion Thompson . 6-2, 190, FR, G. 4-star recruit out of Link Academy (same at Ethan Taylor and CJ Medlock). Did most of his damage with 20 points against Indiana but against both UVA & IU: 26 MIN, 13 PTS, 9-20 FG, 4-9 3 FG, 1.5 REB, 4.5 AST, 2 TO. Key Storylines Matchup of coaching legends. This game will serve as a tiebreaker of sorts as the seventh game between Arkansas’ John Calipari and MSU’s Tom Izzo. Izzo, of course, has been at MSU for each of these games while Calipari has moved around a bit. This is the second matchup with Calipari at Arkansas. The Spartans defeated the Razorbacks 69-66 in the Breslin Center last November. Calipari won the first matchup back in 2008 when he was at Memphis. His Tigers defeated Izzo’s Spartans 92-74 in the Sweet 16. Then, when Calipari was at Kentucky, the two coaches split four games in the Champions Classic between 2013 and 2022. Will the Spartans be close to full strength? Michigan State was down two starters in their win over Detroit Mercy as Jordan Scott sat out with a shoulder injury and Coen Carr was held out with knee tendinitis. Both players saw the floor in MSU’s loss at Tennessee so it will be interesting to see if they are able to go on Thursday. Carr has been a little slow out of the gate this year and perhaps the tendinitis has factored into this. Scott is active on both ends of the floor and was a major defensive presence in the Spartans’ Champions Classic win over Duke. MSU also struggled to put UDM away in Scott’s and Carr’s absence so it may not bode well against a very talented Arkansas team if these two can’t go. Matching up with Richmond, in particular, probably becomes increasingly tougher without Carr and / or Scott. Battle of the bigs. Michigan State has had concerns at the 5-spot since the exhibition season and has seen Anton Bonke go from starter to limited minutes off the bench. Arkansas has three guys in Muurinen, Bowser, and Maker (off the bench) who will challenge MSU on the interior. Will the Spartan bigs be ready for this one? Will MSU show up hungry? Or will they play like they already ate the whole turkey and are ready for a nap on the coach? Fat and sassy as Izzo might say. Michigan State is 5-1, which is probably what many fans might have expected through six games. But we’ve certainly seen some different versions of this Spartans’ team so far this year. There was an impressive defensive effort and some freshmen who looked ready for the bright lights against Duke. Then we saw a school record for three pointers broken against Northern Iowa. We also saw a Detroit Mercy team that had been really struggling to shoot go 10-24 on their three pointers as the winless Titans hung around for far too long against the Spartans. Worst was the debacle in Knoxville, MSU’s only loss, that set the game back to the days of the peach basket. Even though Arkansas has yet to really hit their stride, if Michigan State does this again, they certainly are not coming out of Detroit with a win. How will this one go, TOC? Anyone going to the game in Detroit?

item.title: With Pac-12 title game out of reach, Texas State football's future looks murky
item.description: Texas State quarterback Brad Jackson (8) walks the field after the win over Washington State at UFCU Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026 in San Marcos, Texas. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) SAN MARCOS - There wasn't much drama in Texas State football's 42-14 win over Washington State on Saturday. The Bobcats knew what they were supposed to do; they knew what they could control to give themselves a shot at playing for the Pac-12 championship. What Texas State (7-4, 5-2 Pac-12) couldn't control was the outcome of No. 17 Boise State's game against San Diego State (6-5, 5-2). It couldn't keep Aztecs wide receiver Jaylon Hawkins from making a spectacular touchdown catch in the fourth quarter. It was helpless as Broncos head coach Spencer Danielson recklessly attempted a fourth down on the opposing 46-yard line despite his team leading 20-19 with 1 minute, 31 seconds left. Boise State (9-2, 6-1) failed to convert and lost 22-20 on a walk-off field goal, ending Texas State's hopes of a conference championship. It'll travel to face Utah State and will play in a bowl game, but after that, the team's future is cloudy. MORE: Texas State misses Pac-12 championship game after shocking Boise State loss "We got to do a good job of retaining guys," Texas State head coach GJ Kinne said. "I know the administration; we got a plan, and they're stepping up, but we might have to step up a little bit more." Texas State receiver Chris Dawn Jr. (1) runs the ball during the game against Washington State at UFCU Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026 in San Marcos, Texas. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Can Texas State retain QB Brad Jackson? It's easy to take Texas State's offense for granted. Taking a step back, what Kinne and his staff have accomplished over four years, despite the turnover that comes with running a mid-major program, is stunning. The Bobcats have averaged more than 35 points per game every season since he took over. They've reached even greater heights in the Pac-12; Texas State is averaging 38.73 points and ranks third in the nation in total offensive yards per contest (511.3). The primary reason for that success, aside from Kinne, is quarterback Brad Jackson returning after his spectacular 2025 debut. Jackson's on pace for 3,000 passing yards and has thrown a career-high 23 touchdowns with two games left - not to mention the 705 yards and 10 touchdowns he's added on the ground. Texas State quarterback Brad Jackson (8) runs the ball for a touchdown during the game against Washington State at UFCU Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026 in San Marcos, Texas. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Jackson will go down as one of, if not the best, players to ever don a Texas State uniform. All his accomplishments make retaining him this offseason a monumental task. item.content:encoded: Texas State quarterback Brad Jackson (8) walks the field after the win over Washington State at UFCU Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026 in San Marcos, Texas. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) SAN MARCOS - There wasn't much drama in Texas State football's 42-14 win over Washington State on Saturday. The Bobcats knew what they were supposed to do; they knew what they could control to give themselves a shot at playing for the Pac-12 championship. What Texas State (7-4, 5-2 Pac-12) couldn't control was the outcome of No. 17 Boise State's game against San Diego State (6-5, 5-2). It couldn't keep Aztecs wide receiver Jaylon Hawkins from making a spectacular touchdown catch in the fourth quarter. It was helpless as Broncos head coach Spencer Danielson recklessly attempted a fourth down on the opposing 46-yard line despite his team leading 20-19 with 1 minute, 31 seconds left. Boise State (9-2, 6-1) failed to convert and lost 22-20 on a walk-off field goal, ending Texas State's hopes of a conference championship. It'll travel to face Utah State and will play in a bowl game, but after that, the team's future is cloudy. MORE: Texas State misses Pac-12 championship game after shocking Boise State loss "We got to do a good job of retaining guys," Texas State head coach GJ Kinne said. "I know the administration; we got a plan, and they're stepping up, but we might have to step up a little bit more." Texas State receiver Chris Dawn Jr. (1) runs the ball during the game against Washington State at UFCU Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026 in San Marcos, Texas. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Can Texas State retain QB Brad Jackson? It's easy to take Texas State's offense for granted. Taking a step back, what Kinne and his staff have accomplished over four years, despite the turnover that comes with running a mid-major program, is stunning. The Bobcats have averaged more than 35 points per game every season since he took over. They've reached even greater heights in the Pac-12; Texas State is averaging 38.73 points and ranks third in the nation in total offensive yards per contest (511.3). The primary reason for that success, aside from Kinne, is quarterback Brad Jackson returning after his spectacular 2025 debut. Jackson's on pace for 3,000 passing yards and has thrown a career-high 23 touchdowns with two games left - not to mention the 705 yards and 10 touchdowns he's added on the ground. Texas State quarterback Brad Jackson (8) runs the ball for a touchdown during the game against Washington State at UFCU Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026 in San Marcos, Texas. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Jackson will go down as one of, if not the best, players to ever don a Texas State uniform. All his accomplishments make retaining him this offseason a monumental task. CBSSports reported last December that the top transfer quarterbacks command around $3.5 million, while the average ranges from $1.5 to $2.5 million. The demand for competent quarterback play in college far outweighs the supply. Power Four schools will back up the Brinks truck to tempt Jackson into transferring, and the Bobcats might not have the resources to match. Last year, Kinne expressed confidence that Jackson would return for 2026. This time, the quarterback did not commit to returning to San Marcos after Texas State's win over Washington State. "That's something I'm not really thinking about," Jackson said. "Right now, I'm focused on where my feet are." Texas State Bobcats head coach Gj Kinne with his family after beating the Fresno State Bulldogs 37-35 at UFCU Stadium in San Marcos, Nov. 14, 2026. (Sara Diggins/Austin American-Statesman) A cloudy crystal ball Jackson isn't the only Bobcat who could search for greener pastures. Losing talented players through the portal isn't out of the norm - in fact, it makes it more impressive that the Bobcats retained so many talented players from 2025. The more burning question is what Kinne himself might do. His name has circulated through the coaching carousel for years, and he could be a candidate for a few openings. TCU fired Sonny Dykes on Sunday and Baylor parted ways with Dave Aranda in October. Kinne's father is a former Baylor linebacker, and he might be considered a candidate along with UTSA's Jeff Traylor and others. Sources told the American-Statesman that as of Saturday, the administration and Kinne have not discussed a contract extension. Jackson said Texas State remains focused on the present and what's at stake. But with one less game left to worry about, the future is approaching sooner than they hoped. "Those conversations will be had whenever they're supposed to be had," Jackson said. Sign up for the Daily Briefing from the Austin American-Statesman. item.title: SEC Championship Race Has an Unexpected Problem Entering Rivalry Week
item.description: Dec 6, 2025; Atlanta, GA, USA; Georgia Bulldogs head coach Kirby Smart lifts the SEC Championship trophy after the game against the Alabama Crimson Tide during the 2025 SEC Championship game at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Brett Davis-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) BIRMINGHAM, Ala. — The Southeastern Conference enters Rivalry Week with one major question still unanswered. Georgia has already secured a place in the SEC Championship Game. However, the identity of its opponent remains uncertain. Alabama, Texas and Tennessee enter the final weekend competing for the remaining berth, creating a complicated situation involving head-to-head results and conference tiebreakers. And the most interesting part might be that some of the deciding games will not feature the three contenders. The SEC championship race extends beyond the contenders Conference championship races usually come down to whether the leading teams win their final games. However, the SEC’s expanded membership and scheduling format have created a more complicated scenario. When teams finish with identical conference records, the league applies a series of tiebreaking procedures. Those include head-to-head results, records against common opponents and, when necessary, the combined conference winning percentage of opponents. Consequently, games involving teams outside the championship race can become important. The Egg Bowl between Mississippi State and Ole Miss is one matchup that could affect the calculations. Why Friday could change everything Texas faces Texas A&M on Friday night, giving the Longhorns an opportunity to influence the championship race before Saturday’s games begin. Meanwhile, Mississippi State and Ole Miss meet earlier Friday. Those results could change the scenarios facing Alabama and Tennessee. The Crimson Tide host Auburn in the Iron Bowl, while the Volunteers visit Vanderbilt. Both programs will enter their games knowing that victories elsewhere could affect their paths to Atlanta. Georgia has a different challenge While its potential opponents navigate complicated scenarios, Georgia can focus on preparing for Georgia Tech. The Bulldogs have already secured their championship game appearance. However, they still have College Football Playoff positioning to protect. A rivalry loss would not eliminate Georgia from the SEC title game, but it could complicate its postseason outlook. The final weekend could deliver an unusual finish The SEC’s championship race has become a reminder that the conference’s expanded format can produce unexpected consequences. Several games may influence which team joins Georgia in Atlanta. And depending on Friday’s results, fans could enter Saturday watching more than their own teams. For Alabama, Texas and Tennessee, the challenge is straightforward on the field: Win the rivalry game. What happens elsewhere could prove just as important. item.title: Nunes ready for Napoli, confirms Maresca
item.description: Nunes ready for Napoli, confirms Maresca Matheus Nunes is back and available for the UEFA Champions League clash with Napoli, Enzo Maresca has confirmed. Men's Team Subscribe to CITY+ for live audio commentary of Napoli clash City return to European action on Tuesday at 20:00 (UK) at the Etihad Stadium with only Antoine Semenyo definitely ruled out of the game against our Italian opponents. Nunes missed Saturday’s 1-1 draw with Fulham in the Premier League but the boss confirmed will be back while other members of the squad will be assessed ahead of the clash. But Semenyo continues his rehabilitation with the winger expected to be out for a few more weeks after picking up an injury in the win over Ipswich in mid-October. “Matheus is back. The only one out is still Antoine,” Maresca said in his pre-match new conference. “The rest we have some doubt, in terms of tightness, amount of games. We have today’s session and then we will decide.” Asked if it was the same injury he had suffered earlier in the season, the City boss added: “No, this one is the ankle but now he’s fine. “It’s normal with the amount of games that we have. That’s why I sometimes rotate players. “We need to think not about sprints but marathons - 65 games. “I would like to use the strongest ones in every game. Then we would destroy them so it’s about managing them in the best way.” With Nunes missing, Abdukodir Khusanov stepped in at right back, while it’s a position that Rico Lewis can also take. “Since we started we used Rico there but also Khusa who can play there,” Maresca added. “I am trying to find the right balance. “If you ask me if Khusa is better at full back or central defender no doubt it’s central defender. “But it depends on the game, the players we have available. Rico has done very good so far.” City are currently seventh in the Champions League having won three of our opening four matches. The top eight progress directly to the last-16 knockout stages while places nine to 24 face an extra two matches in the play-offs. Maresca’s first priority is making sure we progress to the next stage of the competition as he aims to get back to winning ways following a frustrating four-game winless run in the Premier League. View full table “We are always looking to win games no matter the competition,” he said. “For sure, the four games in a row in the Premier League that we didn’t win has been a shame. “Tomorrow we have a chance to win the game and continue our path in the Champions League that at the moment has been very good. “First of all, it’s important to qualify and then probably, if you are not able to finish in the top eight, you have two more games that with the amount of games that we have, it’s always important to reduce games. “So the target is to try and finish in the top eight.” BE AT CITY V NAPOLI! item.title: Patrick Mahomes had a three-word reaction to 49ers RT Colton McKivitz’s devastating injury
item.description: Photo by Chris Unger/Getty Images Kansas City Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes sent a message to the fans after watching the gruesome injury suffered by San Francisco 49ers RT Colton McKivitz. The Chiefs are securing their status as one of the favourites for Super Bowl LXI, improving their record to 8-2 with a 34-7 win over the Arizona Cardinals on November 22. They still don’t have the best record, as the San Francisco 49ers improved to 9-1 with a 35-10 win over the Minnesota Vikings. Unfortunately, the 49ers’ status as favourites will come under question now after they lost starting RT McKivitz for the season after suffering a gruesome ankle dislocation that has gone viral. Patrick Mahomes sends support to Colton McKivitz after brutal leg injury Mahomes took to social media after the injury happened live on-air during the second quarter of the 49ers-Vikings clash, asking for prayers for the 30-year-old tackle. “Prayers up man.” Even though the Chiefs and 49ers could be Super Bowl opponents at the end of the year given their respective successes in their conferences, Mahomes’ kind words show how the fraternity of NFL players is rooting for each other’s health and safety. McKivitz was having a career year, ranking No. 7 in PFF among tackles with an 82.8 grade while also being ranked as the second-best run blocker among tackles with an 88.8 grade. The unproven Vederian Lowe will be expected to step up and be strong enough to keep the 49ers afloat. McKivitz has previously also played in a Super Bowl against Mahomes and the Chiefs, starting in what wound up being a 25-22 OT loss at Super Bowl LVIII. The 49ers cannot replace the player they have lost on-field, but it’s clear Mahomes is more concerned with the player’s personal safety before any competitive bad blood could come between them. Hopefully, McKivitz can make a full recovery and help the 49ers next season as a core player. He has been a one-team man since joining the team as a fifth-round draft pick in 2020, earning his way into being a starter and one of their most productive tackles. item.title: Infantino’s $20bn World Cup sell-off plan was to run for up to 96 years, documents show
item.description: Management team were in line for huge payouts Fifa denies Infantino would have profited from plan Gianni Infantino’s failed Fifa Forward Enterprise plan could have locked football in for up to 96 years while paying its management up to 5% of the scheme’s multibillion-pound value, according to documents seen by the Guardian. Previously undisclosed communications by Fifa and Thrive Capital, the lead investor for the proposal, cast fresh light on the deal to sell off football’s crown jewels. They outline a plan, produced days before July’s final of the 2026 World Cup, to profit from the sport’s burgeoning commercial revenues for almost a century. Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: Captain Spence inspires Spurs shock win at City and Lionesses impress
item.description: We may have a proper title race on our hands as City and Chelsea drop points and LCL strengthen their grip on third place Drew Spence rolled back the years with a vintage performance as her Tottenham side produced a shock 3-1 victory away against the defending champions, Manchester City. The 34-year-old marshalled the midfield and then had the vision to thread an outstanding through ball that split the City defence and found the run of Matilda Vinberg, who put Spurs 2-1 up. “She’s unbelievable. There are so many more gears in Drew and I wish I’d been able to work with her a bit earlier [in my career] because her leadership is second to none,” the Tottenham head coach, Martin Ho, said of the club captain. “Her performance levels, since I’ve been here, week on week have grown. She is covering every blade of grass and leads by example. For me, she’s one of the best midfielders in the league.” Tom Garry Match report: Manchester City 1-3 Tottenham Continue reading...

item.title: Inside Fifa and US Soccer’s plan for 2031 World Cup: ‘the largest women’s sporting event in history’
item.description: The US-led four-country bid will be confirmed in Zurich on Monday, projecting record-setting total revenues of $4bn The biggest and most lucrative event in the history of women’s sport will be confirmed at an Extraordinary Fifa Congress in Zurich on Monday, with a joint bid from the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica to host the 2031’s Women’s World Cup to be formally ratified by a vote of Fifa’s 211 member associations. In the bid book submitted to Fifa last year the prospective hosts pledged to generate total revenues of $4bn if awarded hosting rights, which would represent a staggering increase on the $570m earnings from the last World Cup held in Australia and New Zealand three years ago, the first women’s tournament to break even. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘Haaland must be worried’: Thierno Barry’s rise has David Moyes purring
item.description: Everton striker has worked hard to find his scoring touch after admitting he hit ‘rock bottom’ at times last season A most unexpected name sits behind the phenomenon Erling Haaland and the £125m proven marksman Alexander Isak in the Premier League goalscoring chart this season. The rise of Thierno Barry may have surprised even the man himself but stands as a fitting reward for single-minded perseverance and the refusal to quit. “Fabulous” was David Moyes’s take on Barry’s last performance for Everton, when a double against Coventry took the striker to 10 goals for the season in all competitions and his team temporarily up to fifth. It was high praise indeed from a manager who does not dispense tributes freely, and can appear to be on the French forward’s case constantly, but was no more than Barry deserved for a display that also featured an assist for Everton’s third goal of the night. His six Premier League goals leave him joint third alongside Evanilson of Bournemouth and Aston Villa’s Nicolas Jackson. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Leeds offer Chelsea a lesson, Newcastle’s summer recruits struggle and Jules Ahoka makes a name for himself What to make of Manchester United’s utterly torrid start under Mauricio Pochettino? To go glass half full as the new head coach had only three days to prepare the side for the trip to Anfield, the hope will be that time will cast the 4-0 humbling from Liverpool as the falsest of false starts. The glass-half-empty scenario, though, is that here was an XI packed with internationals that had zero clue how to sort out a dire beginning themselves. Leny Yoro’s very early red card may have been questionable but for the wall to evaporate and allow Dominik Szoboszlai’s subsequent free-kick to arrow home was damning evidence of how immature Pochettino’s new charges are. From here it became a debacle and the players, if they have anything about them, need to apologise to the head coach, hold a meeting between themselves and demand they start taking responsibility. If not, United are heading only one way: down. Jamie Jackson Match report: Liverpool 4-0 Manchester United ‘It’s painful for me’: Pochettino criticises Yoro red card decision Continue reading...

item.title: 'We feel the pain': Pochettino on 4-0 defeat at Liverpool to start Manchester United era – video
item.description: Liverpool thrashed 10-man Manchester United 4-0 at Anfield on Sunday to climb to fourth in the Premier League. But the defeat left United 19th, only one point above bottom-placed Crystal Palace. There was no new manager bounce for Mauricio Pochettino, who saw Leny Yoro sent off in the eighth minute for a last-ditch foul on Alexander Isak. Pochettino accepted full responsibility for the loss, but claimed the dismissal was wrong and United should have had a penalty moments earlier for a Jérémy Jacquet challenge on Bryan Mbeumo. 'It was a desperate take,"' writes Andy Hunter at Anfield. Read the full match report here Continue reading...

item.title: Liverpool hand Pochettino nightmare Manchester United start after Yoro sees red
item.description: Green shoots of recovery have lasted longer in a blast furnace than in the Mauricio Pochettino era at Manchester United. On another abysmal Anfield day for the fallen giants of Manchester, Pochettino endured a baptism of fire from the eighth minute onwards when Leny Yoro was sent off for denying Alexander Isak a clear goalscoring opportunity. Liverpool would not be denied anything else while tormenting their old rivals yet again. Andoni Iraola indulged in his first fist-pumps towards the Kop after an utterly dominant, comfortable win illuminated by Rio Ngumoha and Florian Wirtz brilliance plus goals from Dominik Szoboszlai and Víctor Muñoz. Liverpool’s two creative forces were also on the scoresheet as Ngumoha became the youngster scorer in the fixture’s Premier League history. Continue reading...

Make no mistake about it, Fabian Hürzeler’s side will play far worse than this over the next few months and win. They are still second in the table. How they left Hull without even a point almost defies belief given the dominance they enjoyed for large parts of the contest. item.title: Robins ‘aims for the stars’ as Stoke dream of Premier League return
item.description: The Championship’s form side climbed to second after holding on resiliently with 10 men to knock Birmingham off the summit There have been false dawns before. Plenty of them. This time last year, with Christmas on the near horizon, Stoke sat second in the Championship table and were beginning to wonder whether they might allow themselves to dream. So hopeless was their subsequent run that by the onset of spring they were forced to consider a potential relegation fight. Experience has taught the benefit of pragmatism, so no one will be getting ahead of themselves just yet. But this weekend was supposed to be the big test for Mark Robins’s team and few considered they would pass it quite so resoundingly. Continue reading...

item.title: César Azpilicueta: ‘At Chelsea a draw was a catastrophe – if you can’t perform, you’re out’
item.description: Former defender reflects on his record-breaking longevity, kicking Eden Hazard in training, and life after retirement César Azpilicueta looks well. César Azpilicueta always looks well – “ah, Captain Handsome,” one Chelsea fan says when told who’s turning up – but today especially, smiling in the sunshine. Strolling in, he eases into an easier chair, golf course spreading out beyond the terrace, west of Madrid, and orders a detox almost as green. It is nearly 20 years since he played his first game and a few months since he played his last, training kit replaced by bermudas, loafers and a polo, a picture of relaxation. So what’s it like not being a footballer? “Well, different,” he says. Then he laughs, which he does a lot. It is not a laugh-your-head-off laugh, more a chuckle, a giggle, as if amused at everything he did. And for all the self-deprecation, the lack of triumphalism, he did everything. Now, at 37, it’s not the same, although there remains much to do, Azpilicueta as understated and quietly busy as ever: “square,” he calls himself. He’s completed an MBA, a sports directorship diploma and there are media offers, a life to live. Matches to play still: against his kids the needle is never far away, he says. And although he hasn’t found a seven-a-side team yet he will. Continue reading...

item.title: Pochettino needs New Manager Bounce to break torrid Manchester United turnover | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Latest hire will depend on fresh faces and time to bed in at Old Trafford where the dugout churn is hardest to budge Everybody knows the pattern. Performances fade. Results falter. A title challenge becomes clinging on for the last Champions League spot becomes mid-table. Or a promising start becomes a troubling dip, becomes a full-on battle against relegation. Fans begin to grumble. The media wonder whether the spark has gone. Players look disaffected. A dressing room, once lost, is seldom rediscovered, and few managers are given the opportunity to find it again. A crisis in football, once acknowledged, is only ever resolved in one way: by the sacking of the manager. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘Fragile’ Chelsea must toughen up after Leeds humiliation, admits Xabi Alonso
item.description: Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United. They were bullied by a rampant Leeds United, who fully merited their first win at Stamford Bridge since going top with a 2-0 victory in December 1999, and can look forward to another season with no European football if they do not sharpen up soon. It is not really worth dwelling on the fact that the second Leeds goal, a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty converted early in an astonishingly one-sided second half, came after Morgan Rogers was harshly penalised for handball. That was a minor detail given the wider picture. Leeds, superbly coached by Daniel Farke and up to sixth after two clinical strikes from Noah Okafor, Calvert-Lewin’s sixth goal of the season and a late effort from Brenden Aaronson, were so dominant that they had no real need for a helping hand from the officials. Continue reading...

item.title: Aston Villa held at home as dogged Sunderland battle for Régis Le Bris
item.description: For Aston Villa , a painful stalemate at home to Sunderland, but for Régis Le Bris and his players, this was another triumph of sorts. The raw numbers spoke volumes of Villa’s struggles against a defence that backed themselves to keep Unai Emery’s side at bay. All but one of Villa’s seven shots on target came from outside the visitors’ box and the one inside it, courtesy of Ian Maatsen, was forgettable. Owing to a summer of change, injuries and Emery resting John McGinn with Tuesday’s game at Galatasaray in mind, Maatsen, incredibly, was the sole survivor in the Villa starting XI from when these sides played out a 4-3 classic seven months ago. Villa were too predictable, short of a spark, someone to unpick an organised back line. Johan Manzambi, Emi Buendía and Alysson all flattered to deceive on an afternoon when Ibrahim Mbaye and McGinn arrived from the bench. Alejandro Garnacho, however, was not involved in Villa’s matchday squad for the second successive match and the Chelsea loanee has played just 38 minutes in the Premier League this campaign. Tammy Abraham, the match-winner in April, was also left out and a January move looks likely. Continue reading...

item.title: Coventry edge thriller to keep Crystal Palace bottom and ruin Thomas Frank’s start
item.description: New manager, new formation, familiar defensive failings. Twice Crystal Palace equalised. They seemed to have stabilised after half-time. But sometimes the rot is so deep-rooted that the new manager bounce manifests as nothing more than it not looking quite as shambolic as it did before. Thomas Frank started with a defeat that means Palace remain bottom of the table having lost five league games in a row. Yet for much of the second half, there had been reasons for Palace optimism. They seemed to have settled better after a ludicrous first half in which neither side looked at all capable of defending. But a triple substitution by Frank Lampard with 20 minutes to go shifted the game back in Coventry’s favour. With five minutes remaining, a long throw arced into the box. Brandon Thomas-Asante headed it goalwards. Dean Henderson got in the way but the ball bounced off him, hit Dwight McNeil and ricocheted in. “We came through with spirit,” Lampard said. “There was good play and a big impact from the subs. It’s a good sign for the squad.” Continue reading...

item.title: Teenage ace Williams-Barnett puts Tottenham on path to win over Ipswich
item.description: Not since the emergence of a certain Harry Kane has there been this much excitement about a player from Tottenham’s academy. On his first senior start, Luca Williams-Barnett showed just why as the 18-year-old became their youngest Premier League goalscorer since Gareth Bale in 2007 before teeing up Dominic Solanke with a mesmerising and match-winning assist against Ipswich. That made it four league victories from their last five matches for Roberto De Zerbi’s side and the Italian could only have enjoyed the view from the stands as he served his one-match touchline ban. Tottenham have struggled to match their London rivals Arsenal and Chelsea’s record of producing homegrown players in recent years but they appear to have struck gold with Williams-Barnett. Continue reading...

item.title: Elliot Anderson halts Manchester City’s losing run but boos greet Fulham draw
item.description: Manchester City are living in Premier League purgatory, without a win in four, but at least against Fulham they ended a three-game losing run. As they await their fate after being found guilty of financial breaches, their form has slumped. This passive draw was met with boos from the home fans. Arguments will be made over Erling Haaland’s disallowed goal but City did not deserve anything more. The Norwegian uncharacteristically missed a number of fine chances as Rodrigo Muniz took advantage of City’s porous defence. They had to rely on Elliot Anderson to get anything out of the fixture. item.title: Training hard and biding his time, Dele Alli has not given up on football yet
item.description: The 30-year-old former England star combines Twitch streaming with working to return to the top as a player Consider the training regime Dele Alli has followed since he left Como 18 months ago and it becomes clear why he takes exception to suggestions he has given up on football in favour of becoming an internet personality. He trains five or six days a week with Connor Peters, an elite performance coach who has worked with players including Trevoh Chalobah. They spend four days on the pitch and days in between in the gym. A typical day begins at 9am with an hour of activation and stretching before Dele heads to non-league Windsor & Eton at 11am, where he trains on the pitches and uses the facilities. Then it’s back home to use his own oxygen chamber and sauna for a recovery session. Continue reading...

item.title: What history tells us about the Premier League table after 10 games of a season
item.description: Past years suggest it is tough to make big positional gains after slow start but that someone now safe will be relegated The Premier League is about to enter the most intense phase of its season. After 10 rounds of fixtures across the past three months there are 10 in the next seven weeks. Yet if you hibernated for winter, most clubs would be in roughly the same position no matter when in spring you emerged. Across the past decade, Premier League teams’ positions changed by an average of 2.6 places between matchweeks 10 and 38. Only 5.5 clubs per season moved by more than three places over the final 28 games, with almost half of the teams (89 out of 200) shifting by a single spot at most. Every club other than Arsenal will be looking to improve their position but they need not trouble themselves too much. History shows they will probably finish 2026-27 close to their current standing. Continue reading...

item.title: Summer signings join Lionel Messi among MLS’s top earners: Takeaways from the league’s salary release
item.description: How much in player salaries did it take to earn a point in the 2026 MLS regular season? The latest batch of salaries lends some insight Lionel Messi has closer company at the top of MLS’s list of highest-paid players, thanks to another pair of former Barcelona attackers. The Inter Miami captain is still comfortably the league’s top earner, on a guaranteed compensation of $28.3m. Robert Lewandowski (Chicago Fire) and Antoine Griezmann (Orlando City) have entered the list with the second and third highest wages, while Atlanta United’s Breel Embolo, another summer signing, ranks fifth on a guaranteed compensation of $10.8m. Second-year LAFC forward Son Heung-min sits fourth on $11.2m. Casimiro, who joined Messi in Miami at the end of his contract with Manchester United, is his team’s fourth top-earner with a guaranteed compensation of $3.54m. This comes after Miami announced his signing as a non-designated player to the surprise of some as the Brazilian arrived on a Bosman transfer rather than a loan-with-purchase, as Rodrigo De Paul had last summer, to keep Miami rules compliant. The MLS Players’ Association lists Casimiro on a base salary of $896,004. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Football’s political gamers face off at Fifa with the real-life final boss
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Although the millions of gamers who are pulling sickies would beg to differ, the release of Grand Theft Auto VI wasn’t the most exciting midnight launch involving a sprawling enterprise full of shady characters. Over in Zurich, the clock also struck 12 on the candidate deadline for next year’s Fifa presidential election, leaving those of us who have no interest in video games with our own chaotic, multi-billion-dollar sandbox where untouchable bosses bend the rules to suit themselves. While online carjackers are busy exploring a “most extraordinarily, indulgently detailed virtual world” , football’s real-life power brokers are gearing up for a March showdown in the actual city of Rabat. When I first saw the photo in yesterday’s Football Daily , I thought Mauricio Pochettino had opted for a short back and sides, presumably to pre-empt him tearing his luscious locks out in frustration at forthcoming poor results/terrible January transfer window/petulant sniping from sulky squad members. Then I realised he was in the back seat, all but entirely obscured by the rear-view mirror, in which he could perhaps see his sense of job satisfaction disappearing …” – Phil Taverner. That photo of Pochettino being chauffeured by a beefy driver answered one of my burning questions: what’s Ange Postecoglou doing these days?” – Mike Wilner (and others). This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden
item.description: The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quickly It’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it. But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”. It’s just a noise, but it’s unmistakably Danny Kelly. He regains the power of speech and follows it up with: “Gooooaaaal … Goalll Stan, Goalll at the Emirates.” Reporter Ian Abrahams and Stan Collymore join the excitement, before Danny comes back: “I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT.” It is such a brilliant piece of radio . From one of the absolute greats. Continue reading...

item.title: Gonzalo García: ‘I love Craven Cottage – the fans can reach out and touch you’
item.description: Spain Under-21 striker admits the pace of the Premier League has surprised him but says he must stay calm over goal drought at Fulham The first thing Rita Hayworth’s great nephew says when he walks in is: “Sorry I’m late.” Gonzalo García is not late, but it’s very like him: he is impeccably polite, accommodating, and there’s an almost gentle quality to him, a calm that’s not common but can help, especially in moments when the pressure builds. There’s a reason one of the coaches standing in the rain by the pitch where Spain’s under‑21s have just finished training says everyone here loves García. The Fulham striker shakes hands, introduces himself and ducks into the dressing room to change; then a few minutes later he’s back, apologising for a wait that wasn’t one. Time to talk, so let’s start with Tinseltown, the family tale. García laughs. His great-aunt, born Margarita Carmen Cansino, was among the biggest stars in Hollywood, although he’s not sure he’s seen any of her films. His grandfather was a surgeon and others in the family followed. His uncles played rugby for Spain, but that wasn’t his thing. As for him, he enrolled in a degree in business management and analytics, and reckons he might have liked law, yet even that wasn’t his chosen field. Continue reading...

item.title: Netflix, Fox and the $2bn bid for the 2030 World Cup that could reshape live sports
item.description: The battle for the US TV rights to the tournament will pit the traditional broadcaster against the ‘whatever-it-takes’ streamer. It could be a tipping point in the industry The awarding of broadcast rights in the United States for this year’s World Cup was a cut-price deal to avoid legal action from the existing rights holders, Fox Sports. This week’s tender process for the 2030 tournament will be anything but. Media rights and broadcast experts canvassed by the Guardian in the US and Europe are united in agreement that Fifa will benefit from the most competitive and expensive auction in the competition’s history. It is expected to fetch between $1.5bn (£1.13bn) and $2bn, with some predicting the outcome could be a landmark moment for the sports and entertainment industry. Continue reading...

item.title: Swing when you’re winning? Biggest leaps across Fifa’s football rankings | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: clubs with roads on their team badges, most and fewest managers per league title, and more Mail us with all of your questions and answers “The Scotland men’s team’s highest Fifa ranking was 13th (in 2007) and the worst was 88th place (in 2005) – a difference of 75 positions,” writes Bogdan Kotarlic. “Is this the biggest gap between the best and worst ranking for one national team?” The gap between Scotland’s best and worst Fifa rankings isn’t the biggest in men’s international football; in fact, Pete Tomlin calculates that a 75-place swing puts them joint 141st with Ghana and Seychelles. And, as Chris Lewis and others point out, there are a couple of other home nations who have had more dramatic swings. Wales and Northern Ireland both moved up 109 places: Wales from 117th to eighth under Gary Speed and then Chris Coleman, Northern Ireland from 129th in 2004 to 20th in 2017. 183 places Montenegro (16th/199th) 165 Kuwait (24/189) 160 Bosnia and Herzegovina (13/173) 155 Cape Verde (27/182) 153 Central African Republic (49/202) 151 Libya (36/187) 146 Equatorial Guinea (49/195) 144 Moldova (37/181) 141 El Salvador (49/190) 136 Cuba (46/182), Slovakia (14/150) Continue reading...

item.title: Reliving the drama: England and Argentina stars watch 1986 classic with fresh eyes
item.description: A new film about the historic World Cup quarter-final clash finds new angles for a new generation “Is there anything new to say about it?” Gary Lineker asked the producer Flora Fernandez-Marengo when she first approached him to take part in The Match, a documentary about the 1986 World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina. Flora told an audience at the London film festival premiere of the film that she played her best card then and showed Lineker an image of Maradona with Queen in 1981, during the band’s tour of Argentina. Maradona wearing a union jack T-shirt and Freddie Mercury an Argentina strip. It worked. Lineker said yes. The rock’n’roll angle, with Brian May as a talking head, is one of the very few details the film-makers added to Andrés Burgo’s book, The Match, on which the documentary is based. The directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco play with the timeline, hopping between past and present across 91 minutes, the exact duration of the match itself. Anecdotes that now form part of Argentina’s football folklore are spliced with excellent archive material. Continue reading...

item.title: Janine van Wyk: ‘Our rooms were empty … no mattresses, no lightbulbs and not a drop of water’
item.description: In an extract from the former South Africa captain’s book, she details less than ideal Wafcon 2006 preparations I was just a year into my international career when we qualified for my first Wafcon, which was then called the African Women’s Championship (AWC) and was held in Nigeria in 2006. I was extremely excited but very nervous to participate in this tournament, more so when it was announced that we would be in the same group as the hosts, and would play them last in the group. As it turned out, it would be the game that decided who finished top of the group. By then we had beaten Algeria 4-0 and Equatorial Guinea 2-0 and had to travel to Delta State to take on the hosts. I’d heard that Nigeria was the toughest country to travel to and I was about to realise why. It’s become common knowledge that South Africans and Nigerians are massive rivals on the football field but also don’t really get on off it. Continue reading...

item.title: Thomas Frank’s to-do list: lift mood, fix defence and fire up Sarr and Mateta
item.description: Seeking redemption after failing at Spurs, newly installed Crystal Palace manager has a tough challenge ahead Thomas Frank promised his wife, Nanna, he would take a year’s sabbatical after being sacked by Tottenham in February , but he couldn’t wait that long. Having received a reported £8m payoff from Spurs, he kept an extremely low profile in the first few months after an experience at the club that sources close to the 53‑year‑old have described as “traumatic”. Frank broke his silence at the start of June with a statement released by the League Managers Association. It said he would cover the World Cup for the BBC (thereby going head-to-head with Ange Postecoglou, his predecessor at Spurs, who worked for ITV) before “experiencing the Tour de France”, a lifelong passion. Frank usually preferred to run to Brentford’s training ground and home matches from his home in East Sheen during a nine‑year spell as assistant and then manager, but he occasionally cycled because it helped to clear his head. Continue reading...

item.title: Echoes of Azteca but not like Argentina: fearless England start afresh in Madrid
item.description: ‘We will not go back on this way of playing,’ says Thomas Tuchel after he delivered response to World Cup critics Thomas Tuchel made defensive substitutions as England protected a lead. He finished with three centre-backs on the pitch. His team could not get out of their half in the final part of the game. So close your eyes and imagine an alternate universe in which James Trafford did not make his stunning double save in stoppage time on Sunday and England had drawn 3-3 with Spain at the Metropolitano Stadium rather than won 3-2 . The reaction would not have been kind because Tuchel has been here before. The head coach wanted to push one particular comparison from the World Cup over the summer. “It was Mexico reloaded,” he said, with a nod towards the 3-2 last-16 win at the Azteca Stadium and it fitted like a glove – down to the detail of Jarell Quansah and red cards. Continue reading...

item.title: Do good club managers necessarily make good international managers? | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: In a mailbag edition of our newsletter, we look at Mauricio Pochettino, Pep Guardiola’s international credentials and the lack of elite English managers Sign up for our free newsletter here Who should replace Mauricio Pochettino as the USMNT manager? – Tom S Although the salary I’m sure will be excellent, I think the US job is going to be a really difficult sell to a top-level coach. The 2030 World Cup is a long way away and I’m not sure the Concacaf Nations League, the Gold Cup or even the 2028 Copa América carry much appeal for a manager with European experience or aspirations. But I’m not entirely sure that sort of coach is necessarily a great idea. The last two World Cups, after all, have been won by low-key coaches who have come from within the federation and have worked with many of the players at youth level. That’s the positive from appointing from within; appointing from without is almost certainly more expensive and there’s the danger the next foreign manager does just what Mauricio Pochettino does, and has his head turned by the first vaguely attractive European job that comes calling. This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Have a question for Jonathan? Email soccerwithjw@theguardian.com , and he’ll answer the best in a future edition. Continue reading...

item.title: Familiarity of Doha drives home just how far Socceroos have come in recent years | Joey Lynch
item.description: There is increasing evidence of an evolution not only in approach but also mentality, highlighted by a return to the scene of Asian Cup heartbreak Last week’s 3-0 dismissal of Qatar at the Abdullah bin Khalifa Stadium marked the first time the Socceroos had returned to the Gulf state since their heartbreaking elimination from the Asian Cup just under three years ago. Back then, coach Graham Arnold called Doha a “home away from home” after they relocated there during the Covid pandemic, and went so far as to suggest that they would have some form of advantage at the 2022 World Cup as a result. Wandering around the city in 2026, memories rush back of Socceroos fans becoming eager participants in the takeover of the city’s souks during the World Cup. So too the feelings of sadness to see the birds still cooped up in small cages at the nearby bird market. It evokes recollections of trips on the red Metro line out to the Al Janoub Stadium in Al Wakrah, aided by the faded posters and stickers celebrating the 2022 tournament’s arrival that to this day can still be seen in shopfronts. There’s the excitement, for some, when a stray cat reminds you just how personable the local felines can be, as well as the sense of unease that remains whenever one pauses to reflect on how all this was built and the hands that did so. Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: Chelsea’s gamble pays off and have Arsenal lost fear factor?
item.description: Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL draw Sonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. Suzanne Wrack Match report: Chelsea 1-0 Manchester City Continue reading...
